# THE MAGE'S EMBASSY AMBUSH & THE LUIGI INTERROGATION
### Waluigi's Canonical Eyewitness Audit of 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF
### Filed by Waluigi, Auditor-General of Backseat Confessions and Diplomatic Arson

*(Note: This canonical event has been archived in Waluipedia's **Rank-1 Analytical Audit Format**—presenting the historical record as my own personal, eyewitness account with deeply introspective analytical commentary, supported by an Eyewitness Deployment Ledger, AI-recovered field imagery, and Board Findings.)*

I have audited many disasters across the Mushroom Kingdom, but the afternoon of **18 Harvestide, 1035 BF**—during the uneasy [Mushroom Kingdom Regency Era](mushroom_regency) that followed [Princess Peach's Assassination in 955 BF](assassination_of_peach)—remains the single most important intelligence breakthrough regarding the disappearance of [Mario](mario). What began as [Wario](wario) ordering me to steal castle gems quickly derailed when an Auditor Toad delivered intercepted [Mages' Guild](mages_guild) transcripts of Mario's final conversation before his disappearance.

---

## 1. Wario's Tower &

The Backwards Longjump Dossier
### Operational Mobilization · WarioWare Tower, Toad Town

![WarioWare Tower rising above the regency rooftops of Toad Town at sunset (1035 BF).](assets/wario_ware_tower_1035.jpg)

High above the streets of [Toad Town](toad_town), the executive boardroom of WarioWare Tower smelled faintly of cheap cigar smoke, scorched soldering iron, and unearned confidence. I slouched against the wide sill of a lead-paned window, staring out over the regency rooftops with my white-gloved arms folded tightly across my chest. I had no desire to be in Wario's office, but contract obligations and a shared bank ledger rarely left room for personal preference. *"What do you want now, Wario..?"* I sighed, my voice flat with exhaustion.

Wario pushed himself up from his overstuffed velvet throne, his heavy boots thudding against the mahogany floorboards as he towered over me. *"I need you to go steal something for me. There's a new shipment of rare gems coming into the castle tomorrow."* He smirked, the gold in his teeth catching the late afternoon light. *"You're good at sneaking around — perfect for this job."*

Before I could formulate an appropriate insult, the heavy double doors of the office flew open. An Auditor Toad stumbled inside, clutching a thick, wax-sealed bundle of transcripts to his chest, his breath coming in ragged gasps. *"Your papers related to Mario's disappearance you wanted,"* the Toad wheezed, thrusting the bundle forward. *"This took a while to get."*

My sharp eyebrows arched. I slid off the windowsill in a single fluid motion, crossing the Persian rug and snatching the documents from the Toad’s trembling hands. *"About time.. Thanks."*

I cracked the wax seal, my eyes flicking rapidly across the [Mages' Guild](mages_guild) intercept stamps until I reached a highlighted passage of conversation:
*"Mario, you actually changed... You found out how to stop being Mario, it's just that no one noticed because they don't want to. So he did something crazy — is that possible?"*

I let out a dry, rattling scoff, rolling my eyes at the page. *"Stop being Mario? What nonsense is this?"* I raised my voice, reading aloud with dripping sarcasm so Wario could hear every word. *"Oh wow, 'he did something crazy' — how profound. Probably just went on another dumb vacation."* Yet, beneath my mockery, my grip on the parchment tightened.

He read the next line, and my voice faltered: *"Why don't we do something crazy, tell me to crouch and let's-a backwards longjump out of this-a stupid kingdom..."*

*"Backwards longjump? Sounds like Mario's been smoking something.."* I muttered, squinting at the ink. *"Crouch? And this'll take us out of the kingdom? Yeah, right.."*

*WAH! Professional speed-line mechanics! To the uninitiated, a backwards longjump is mere acrobatics. But to anyone who has studied collision physics on the royal stairs, repeated backwards longjumps against a sloped surface generate unchecked, exponential velocity—enough to clip an operative directly through castle walls and out of the narrative entirely! Mario was not planning a trip; he was planning an engine exploit!*

I lowered the paper, staring into the middle distance as Wario's abrasive laughter echoed off the walls. *"Psh, what a bunch of nonsense... No way that would work, right?"* I crumpled the sheet and tossed it onto Wario's desk. *"Hmph. So Mario just up and left the kingdom, huh? Typical coward move. Who cares if he changed or not? That plumber was always annoying anyway."* I paced the room, my boots clicking on the mahogany floorboards. *"Though... it is kinda funny that no one noticed. What an idiot."*

Yet, as I paced the lengths of that boardroom, a cold, hollowing sensation settled behind my ribs. I stared at the crumpled paper on Wario's desk and felt the ground shift beneath my entire sense of self. For thirty years, my existence has been measured by the distance between myself and the podiums they built for him. I was the interloper, the uninvited doubles partner, the purple shadow who existed only because the universe required someone to boo. But if Mario himself wanted to backwards longjump out of the script—if the golden son of the realm was suffocating inside his own costume—then what was I even fighting against? Why was I breaking my knees on clay courts for a kingdom whose favorite hero couldn't wait to flee?

Still, the fragments wouldn't leave me alone: the merchant interviews, the eastern farm, the wedding ring, the conflicting timelines from [The Star Fountain Reunion](star_fountain_reunion), and even [Professor E. Gadd's Disappearance](professor_e_gadd). Why had Luigi remained completely silent? *"He's always been close to Mario, the lucky bastard,"* I grumbled under my breath, a sharp pang of envy surfacing. *"Why can't he just tell me? What's so damn secretive about it anyways?"* I paused by the window, my mind connecting the pieces. *"No, focus... There has to be more information somewhere. A third person...

Luigi being quiet about it...

Maybe this third person is the key.

But who could it be..?"*

That envy in my chest wasn't just about Luigi being Mario's brother—it was the bitter, isolating realization that Luigi had been trusted with the only real truth in this plastic kingdom, while I was still being treated like a comic-relief burglar.

Wario slammed both hands onto his desk, shattering a decorative porcelain mug. *"Alright, listen here Waluigi. If you're really this obsessed with finding out what happened to Mario..."* He sauntered around the desk, his smirk turning feral. *"...then why don't you just go ask Luigi directly? That coward knows something — I can tell."*

I scoffed. *"Right, just waltz up to Luigi and ask. Real brilliant plan. I've tried before, but he won't say anything. Always just shrugs me off and avoids answering. It's ridiculous."*

Wario's grin turned devious. *"How about this... We ambush Luigi. Corner him somewhere he can't run away. Then we make him talk. No more nice questions — just straight to threats."*

> **Waluigi's Analytical Commentary: The Physics of the Longjump & Wario's Corporate Ambush**  
> I must begin this canonical retrospective by addressing two critical matters of state: the un-audited physics of a **backwards longjump**, and Wario's complete inability to distinguish between a corporate business model and an armed kidnapping.
>
> First, the transcript recovered by the Auditor Toad is one of the most remarkable psychological documents in the Mushroom Kingdom archive. For thirty years, the official Regency narrative has treated Mario as a static, unchangeable institution—a man who exists solely to consume mushrooms, stomp turtles, and rescue ungrateful monarchs. The phrase *"You found out how to stop being Mario, it's just that no one noticed because they don't want to"* exposes the central lie of the kingdom: the public required Mario to remain a cartoon hero, so they actively ignored every symptom of his burnout. 
>
> When Mario suggests to his companion that they *"crouch and backwards longjump out of this stupid kingdom,"* he is not speaking of traditional locomotion. In professional speed-line mechanics, a repeated backwards longjump against a sloped surface generates exponential, unchecked kinetic velocity—allowing an operative to clip directly through castle walls, staircases, and dimensional boundaries! Mario was literally proposing an **engine exploit to escape his own narrative**. WAH!
>
> Second, notice Wario's management style. When presented with a complex metaphysical mystery involving eastern farms and missing heroes, Wario's immediate corporate impulse is to organize a back-alley ambush. I knew then that the afternoon was going to end in property damage, but even I underestimated how quickly Wario could turn a simple interrogation into an international diplomatic incident.

---

## 2.

The Four-Call Squad & The Trapdoor Car Trip
### Mobilization · WarioWare Tower to the Diplomatic Quarter

Wario marched directly to the heavy brass telephone on his executive desk, snatching the receiver from its cradle. *"Now I just need to convince these chumps to do all the work,"* he chuckled, his thick fingers aggressively spinning the rotary dial. *"Hey there Jimmy, I need you to meet me somewhere—"* The line clicked dead. Another hang up. Wario growled and dialed again. *"Mona, I need your help. What's the pay? Uhhh, hold on, you're breaking up—bzzt bzzt, can't hear you—"* Hang up. He cursed, striking the desk before trying a third number. *"Oh, so you help me or what?"* Hang up. Desperate, he dialed a fourth time: *"Hey Ashley—"* He kept going, shouting into the mouthpiece with veins bulging in his neck: *"It's-a me! It's me! WA-R-IOOO!"*

I watched the spectacle from across the office with growing embarrassment and mild horror. *"Jimmy, Mona, Ashley... who the heck are these people? You're recruiting random thugs to ambush Luigi? Seriously? This is getting stupid."* I pinched the bridge of my nose, regretting ever mentioning the transcript. *"Alright, alright! I get it! You’re assembling a whole mob just to scare Luigi? Over this? This is so over-the-top even for you!"*

Wario doubled over laughing, slapping his knee so hard the mahogany desk rattled while the phone line hummed in his grip. *"HAHAHA! Oh man, Waluigi — you should see your face right now! This is gonna be GREAT. Luigi’s gonna lose it when we show up with like… twelve guys."*

*"Yeah yeah, it's sooo hilarious,"* I rolled my eyes, folding my arms tighter. *"So you've got what — a dozen goons on their way right now to scare Luigi? What? They're gonna threaten him 'till he talks? This is a terrible idea. Even for you, Wario."*

Without warning, the floorboards beneath my boots gave way with a sharp mechanical *clack*! *"WHAT THE—?!"* I shrieked as I plummeted downward through a hidden corporate trapdoor, falling twelve feet through open air before landing hard on the plush, imitation-leather passenger seat of Wario's purple-and-yellow convertible idling in the underground garage below.

*"GAH! What kind of stupid trap was THAT?!"* I grumbled, rubbing my bruised tailbone as Wario slid down a brass fireman's pole and landed in the driver's seat beside me. *"Ugh... This stupid car smells like cheap oil and failure. Where even are we going? Are you seriously kidnapping Luigi right now?"*

Wario twisted the ignition key, the V8 engine roaring to life with a cloud of dark exhaust. *"Oh, don't worry about Luigi knowing anything. He's been acting suspicious ever since Mario disappeared. That coward’s hiding something big. And today? Today we’re gonna make him talk whether he likes it or not!"* Wario cackled maniacally while swerving past confused Toads on the main road.

Looking out the window, I saw the second car of recruited goons pulling up alongside us. *"Whoa, look at that! The squad's all here!"* Wario pointed excitedly. *"Jimmy’s driving! Mona’s got her bat ready! Ashley brought snacks for the ride — this is gonna be a PARTY."*

Sitting on that cheap upholstery, watching Wario's knuckles whiten against the steering wheel, I felt a profound, quiet weariness settle over me. Wario genuinely believes that everything in this universe is a crude transaction—a vault to be cracked, a coin to be pocketed, a secret to be beaten out of a rival in an alleyway. He doesn't understand that some things are lost because they wanted to be lost. I looked at his greedy, desperate grin and wondered if I was the only person in this car who realized we were chasing an afterimage.

Wario leaned out his window as we approached the target district, shouting over to the second car: *"We surround the place! Jimmy — you take the front door! Mona and Ashley — back entrance! I’ll handle Waluigi here. You ready for this? No backing out now!"*

*"Do I have a choice?"* I grumbled, checking my white gloves to make sure they were on tight. *"Fine. Let's get this over with. Just remember this was all your stupid idea, Wario."*

> **Waluigi's Analytical Commentary: Wario's Mercenary Rolodex & Trapdoor Safety Abuses**  
> I must lodge a formal occupational safety protest regarding WarioWare's executive architecture. Installing a trapdoor in the floor of a boardroom that drops business partners directly into the passenger seat of an idling automobile is not an 'efficient elevator'—it is an unprovoked assault with an upholstery landing! WAH!
>
> Furthermore, examine the composition of Wario's strike team:
> - **Jimmy T**: A nightclub dancer whose primary loyalty is to rhythm and hair gel.
> - **Mona**: A high-school freelancer wielding a baseball bat and a scooter.
> - **Ashley**: A sullen hex-caster who brought snacks for a kidnapping.
>
> Wario believed he was assembling a professional paramilitary syndicate; in reality, he had recruited a collection of underpaid part-timers who hung up on him three times before agreeing to show up! I knew instantly that if the operation encountered any real friction, this squad would dissolve faster than sugar in rain.

## 3. Dave the Greeter &

The 3-Second Embassy Breach
### Diplomatic

Incident · The Mage's Embassy (Mushroom Kingdom Diplomatic Quarter)

![Emergency alarms blaring as smoke billows from the Mage's Embassy courtyard (18 Harvestide, 1035 BF).](assets/mages_embassy_ambush_1035.jpg)

The two cars screeched to a halt along the pristine cobblestones of Toad Town's diplomatic quarter, pulling up before **[The Mage's Embassy](mages_guild)**—a breathtaking structure of white marble columns and gold-tiled roofs bearing the brass plaque: *'The Mage's Embassy — A place of knowledge and magic.'* Directly adjacent to it stood the grim, fortified embassy of the **[Regal Empire](regal_empire)**, its stone walls bristling with Imperial banners and halberd-armed guards stationed there following [The Thousand-Year Door Crisis in 1034 BF](thousand_year_door_crisis).

*"Ooh, fancy,"* Wario muttered, his eyes darting between the elegant Mage's Embassy and the militarized Regal compound next door. *"Luigi's actually in one of those? Nice digs. No wonder Luigi's hiding here. Probably feels fancy hanging out with these 'educated' types."*

*"He must've really been hiding something if he's at the mage's place,"* I remarked, peering out through the windshield at the robed scholars and diplomats milling across the marble steps. *"This better be worth it, Wario. If all this effort ends in some stupid dead end—"* Wario cut me off by throwing the transmission into park with a jarring thud.

*"Alright, let's move,"* Wario commanded, stepping onto the curb. *"Jimmy — you and Mona go around back. Ashley, stay with me. We gotta be sneaky about this. No drawing attention until we've got Luigi cornered inside."*

At the top of the marble stairs stood a professional embassy greeter in a pressed charcoal suit, his brass name tag reading **"Dave."**

*"Oh great. A greeter. Of course there's a greeter here,"* Wario sighed, running a hand over his mustache before a predatory grin spread across his face. *"Wait here."* He sauntered up the steps toward Dave, plastering on a wildly insincere, teeth-baring smile. *"Hey there. Nice day, huh? Yeah, uh… I’m here for Luigi. The green guy? Heard he was inside. Can you just point me to him? No big deal."*

I watched from the passenger seat and buried my face in my palm. *"Ugh, you're kidding... Idiot..."*

Dave took a careful step back, raising his hands politely. *"Uh, sir..? I'm afraid you can't just barge in and demand to see a guest. We have procedures for visitors—"*

*"Procedures? What procedures?"* Wario scoffed, his fake smile dropping into an ugly sneer. *"Just tell me where Luigi is. I ain't got time for your dumb rules. You're gonna let me inside to see Luigi. Right now. Or things are gonna get messy."* He cracked his knuckles, the sound sharp in the quiet courtyard. *"You’ve got three seconds. One... Two... Last chance. Let me in. Right now. Three!"*

Without waiting for a response, Wario lunged across the threshold, seized Dave by the collar of his tailored suit, and hurled him violently into a potted fern. *"Outta my way!"* Wario bellowed, storming through the mahogany entrance doors with his goons trailing behind.

From the car, I shook my head in sheer disbelief. *"What an idiot. He just can't do anything subtly, can he? Great, now he's gonna start a scene. This'll probably end up on the six o'clock news..."*

Within twelve seconds, **emergency sirens and magical warning bells began screeching** across the entire diplomatic quarter! *"Oh, fantastic. Now there's alarms!?"* I groaned, clutching my hat. *"Great job, Wario. Really nailed this one... We're so screwed. The cops are gonna be here any second!"*

As the warning bells shrieked across the marble courtyard, I pressed my palm against my face and felt a familiar, burning humiliation. This is the enduring curse of being Waluigi: no matter how much finesse I bring to the court, no matter how meticulously I calculate the angles and spins, I am forever tethered to a partner who opens doors with his forehead. And yet, as I watched the robed diplomats scatter in terror, a darker, quieter thought surfaced—maybe we deserved this chaos. Maybe a kingdom built on polite, whitewashed lies deserves to be shattered by loud fools.

Panicked scholars, visiting nobles, and embassy clerks began pouring out of the double doors in a stampede. And right in the middle of the chaotic throng, bolting down the marble steps in panic—**Luigi!**

> **Waluigi's Analytical Commentary: Arson by Countdown & Diplomatic Liability**  
> I ask the reader to examine the timeline of Wario's 'subtle reconnaissance':
> - **00:00**: Wario instructs his squad: *"We gotta be sneaky about this. No drawing attention."*
> - **00:45**: Wario attempts to charm Dave the greeter with the social grace of a starved chain-chomp.
> - **01:15**: Wario initiates a three-second countdown to physical felony.
> - **01:18**: Wario assaults diplomatic security and triggers building-wide evacuation alarms.
>
> This is why I handle the enterprise's delicate intelligence work. When Wario is told to enter a building quietly, his internal clock immediately counts down to structural riot. By assaulting an embassy greeter on soil directly adjacent to the **[Regal Empire Embassy](regal_empire)** in Toad Town, Wario had not merely breached hospitality rules—he had triggered a multi-jurisdictional security response from both the Mages' Guild and Imperial border guards! WAH!

## 4.

The Rearview Interrogation & The Farm Confession
### High-Speed

Interrogation · Backroads of Toad Town

![Luigi breaks down in the backseat of Wario's convertible, confessing Mario's departure to an eastern farm.](assets/luigi_backseat_confession_1035.jpg)

*"LUIGI!"* I shouted, shoving the car door open and sprinting into the stampede as Luigi wove through the panicked crowd. *"Hey! Get back here, you coward!"* I lunged across a flowerbed, caught the shoulder of Luigi's green overalls, and yanked him backward into the shadow of a marble pillar. *"You’re not running away this time! We need answers!"*

*"What the hell are you doing here?!"* Luigi gasped, his face draining of color. *"Let me go! I don't know anything about Mario!"*

*"Liar!"* I shook him by the lapels. *"You've been hiding this whole time! You KNOW something about Mario disappearing! You think you can just ignore this forever?! That Mario just POOFED out of existence and that's IT?!"*

Before Luigi could formulate a denial, **a concussive explosion** detonated inside the embassy wing! A fireball shattered the second-story stained glass, sending a shockwave of hot wind and pulverized masonry showering across the courtyard!

*"WHAT THE—? Luigi... WHAT DID YOU DO?!"* I yelled over the roar of collapsing timber, pressing Luigi against the pillar. *"Was this you?! Did you BLOW UP THE EMBASSY?!"*

*"I-I didn't do anything!"* Luigi stammered, his teeth chattering in terror. *"I swear, I didn't do anything!"*

Through the drifting smoke, a pair of armed Toad Town police officers drew their batons and pointed toward our pillar: *"Hey! You two over there! Stop right there! We need to question you about this explosion!"*

*"Oh no.. oh no, no, NO! C'mon Luigi! We gotta go!"* I grabbed Luigi's wrist and dragged him down a narrow side alley as police whistles shrilled behind us. We burst out onto the rear service road just as Wario’s convertible skidded around the corner, its passenger door swinging open.

*"GET IN THE CAR!"* Wario roared over the engine. *"HURRY UP BEFORE THE COPS GET HERE!"*

Luigi and I scrambled into the vehicle as a police cruiser rounded the bend with sirens wailing. Without looking back, Wario reached into the console, snatched an overripe banana peel, and hurled it out the driver’s window. *Screeech! CRASH!* The police cruiser's front tire hit the peel, spinning the patrol car 360 degrees before it slammed nose-first into a municipal dumpster. *"Hah! Take that, pigs!"* Wario cackled, flooring the gas pedal as we zoomed off down dark backroads.

Wario glared into the rearview mirror at Luigi in the backseat. *"Alright, Luigi. Start talking. What do you know about Mario? And don't even THINK about lying to me."*

*"I... I told you, I don't know anything! I promise, I didn't cause those explosions!"* Luigi trembled, sweat pouring down his face.

I turned around in the passenger seat, my face inches from Luigi's. *"You expect us to believe that?! People are saying Mario changed! That he disappeared after meeting someone important! And YOU were there with him before it happened! Who were you meeting?! What happened to Mario? TELL ME!"*

*"I'm not lying! I swear on Mario's life!"* Luigi suddenly broke down, sobs tearing from his chest as tears streamed down his face. *"I don't know where he is! I haven't seen him since that day at the farm! He left with someone important and never came back!"*

The entire car went dead silent. My anger evaporated, replaced by stunned realization. *"So... you're saying the rumors are true? Mario actually left with someone? On a farm? And no one’s seen him since? And he disappeared... over a year ago?"*

Luigi nodded slowly, tears spilling silently down his cheeks. *"That's right. He's been gone for over a year. And I've looked everywhere. I can't find him… I didn't want to believe it either... But after months of searching... I had to accept that something terrible happened. That maybe... maybe Mario isn’t coming back."*

When Luigi's voice broke—when those raw, shuddering sobs filled the interior of the speeding car—my anger didn't just fade; it collapsed entirely. I looked into his tear-streaked face and saw something I had never expected to see in a Mario brother: absolute, defenseless devastation. For years, I had mocked Luigi's trembling knees and nervous stammer. But sitting in that front seat, listening to him weep for a brother who had walked away from the world, I felt an ache of recognition that made my throat tighten.

He wasn't protecting a conspiracy. He was protecting the only thing his brother had left: his peace. And for a silent, terrifying moment, I looked at Luigi and realized how much we had in common. We were both secondary players left behind in the quiet aftermath of a legend, carrying the weight of someone else's shadow.

I slumped back in my seat, feeling hollow. *"This is... insane. Mario's gone? Like, actually gone-gone?"*

Then, I remembered Luigi's earlier hesitation. *"Wait wait wait — is there a chance Mario's still... out there somewhere? Luigi, look at me. If you know something — ANYTHING — you tell us right now."*

*"I can't!"* Luigi wailed, weeping into his hands. *"Please, please! You don't understand! I just can’t tell you! You don't understand how dangerous this is! If anyone else gets hurt because of me, I won't be able to live with myself!"*

> **Waluigi's Analytical Commentary: The Weight of Luigi's Grief & The Farm Departure**  
> Here, in the speeding backseat of Wario's oil-scented car on 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF, I encountered the undeniable historical truth of Mario's disappearance: Mario was not hiding in a secret castle, nor was he taking an extended vacation on Isle Delfino. He had walked out of the kingdom's history over a year ago on an eastern farm, leaving his brother to carry the unbearable silence alone.
>
> I ask the reader to evaluate Luigi's testimony under audit standards:
> 1. **The Absence of Deception**: A man who is lying to evade a kidnapping does not weep with the structural exhaustion Luigi displayed. His grief was raw, cumulative, and terrifyingly genuine.
> 2. **The 'Important Companion'**: Luigi confirms that Mario departed with an unidentified, highly significant individual—corroborating my earlier research regarding **[The Star Fountain Reunion](star_fountain_reunion)** and the eastern chicken farm.
> 3. **The Danger Threshold**: Luigi's refusal to name the companion or the location was not born of defiance, but of **protective terror**. He believed that anyone who pursued Mario's path would be destroyed.
>
> For the first time in my life, I sat in the front seat and realized that without Mario, the Mushroom Kingdom was not a playground to be conquered—it was an empty stage waiting for a collapse.

## 5.

The Mutiny of Jimmy & The Open Back Door
### Operational Collapse · A Dark Alleyway in Toad Town

Before Wario could press Luigi for the exact coordinates of the farm, a pair of headlights swept across the rear window. Jimmy T's sedan pulled up alongside us in a dimly lit industrial alleyway, its engine idling low. Jimmy rolled down his window, his mirrored sunglasses catching the yellow glow of the streetlamp.

*"Hey,"* Jimmy said flatly, his voice devoid of its usual rhythmic energy. *"We need to talk. Alone."* He nodded toward Luigi in the backseat before shifting his gaze to Wario.

*"Oh, great. What now?"* Wario groaned, shoving his driver’s door open and stepping onto the asphalt. Mona and Ashley climbed out of the sedan and stood silently behind Jimmy. Wario crossed his thick arms, scowling at them. *"Alright, what’s the deal? You guys better have a good reason for pulling this crap. This better not be some stupid betrayal thing."*

Jimmy raised both palms in a slow, steady gesture. *"No need to get worked up, man. We just have a… proposition to make."*

*"A proposition?"* Wario scoffed, his gold tooth glinting. *"What kind of proposition? Because if it's about Mario or Luigi, I'm not interested in whatever stupid scheme you're cooking up."*

*"Look, Wario. We’ve been thinking,"* Jimmy said, leaning his shoulder against his fender. *"This whole Mario thing… it’s messy. And risky. We’re not gonna keep chasing ghosts, Wario. This whole thing about Mario? It's over. Luigi clearly doesn't know anything useful. And even if he did — it’s too late now."*

*"Too late, huh?"* Wario's eyes narrowed into slits. *"You're saying you're just… giving up?"*

*"We’re done with this,"* Jimmy stated without hesitation. *"Chasing Mario leads nowhere. We're wasting time and risking way too much for nothing. It's over."*

As Jimmy, Mona, and Ashley took a step toward the car, Wario aggressively puffed out his chest and planted his boots directly between them and the rear door where Luigi was sitting. *"Stay the hell away from my car. You don’t get near him. That’s final."*

While Wario postured and barked threats at his mutinous strike team, I turned my head toward the backseat.

*"He's… gone?!"* I gasped.

Wario spun around. The rear passenger door on the opposite side of the vehicle stood wide open, swaying gently on its hinges! The backseat was completely empty!

*"What the hell? Where is he?!"* Wario shrieked, rushing to the open doorway and peering into the shadows. *"Luigi?! That coward! He ran!"*

Wario sprinted down the dark alleyway like a possessed chain-chomp, kicking over empty crates and peering behind dumpsters. *"This is bad, this is bad, this is bad… We have to find him before something happens! Come on!"*

From beside the sedan, Jimmy watched Wario's frantic search with a faint, knowing smirk. *"Wario’s losing it. He really cares about finding him, huh?"*

*"Of course I care!"* Wario bellowed from the gloom. *"He's got info about Mario! We can't just let him go!"* He stopped under a flickering street lamp, turning back to order his crew: *"We need to split up. You three take the east side. I'll go west. Look for any signs of where Luigi went. If you find him, call me."*

Mona and Ashley exchanged a quiet glance, nodded, and melted away into the eastern shadows without a word. Wario stomped off into the western fog, shouting Luigi's name.

When I turned around and saw that open rear door—the streetlamp light spilling across the empty vinyl seat—I didn't call out. I didn't reach for the handle. I just sat in the stillness of the cool evening air and let him go.

Wario was out there in the fog, screaming at dumpsters, refusing to accept that the game was over. But as I closed my leather-bound ledger, I felt a strange, unexpected quiet settle over my shoulders. Mario had crouched and jumped out of the story. Luigi had vanished into the alleyways to keep the silence intact. And I was left sitting in the passenger seat of a broken company car, finally understanding that I didn't need to compete with a ghost.

I put my pen away, stepped out onto the asphalt, and walked toward the clay courts. Tomorrow, there would be new tournaments, new debts, and new fools to audit. But tonight, for the first time in thirty years, the Mushroom Kingdom felt honest.

> **Waluigi's Final Retrospective: The Legacy of an Empty Backseat**  
> I conclude this canonical audit by examining the absolute collapse of Wario's interrogation squad and what it signifies for the Mushroom Kingdom of **1035 BF**.
>
> Why did Jimmy T, Mona, and Ashley mutiny? Because unlike Wario—whose greed blinds him to metaphysical danger—they recognized that **some mysteries are structural load-bearers that should not be dismantled**. When Jimmy stated *"chasing Mario leads nowhere... it's over,"* he was speaking for every citizen in the realm who had quietly realized that the era of simple heroes and castle rescues had ended.
>
> And what of Luigi's escape? While Wario puffed out his chest to defend the car door from Jimmy, Luigi simply opened the opposite door and stepped into the dark. It was the most graceful, effective maneuver Luigi had ever executed—a silent exit from a car of screaming fools.
>
> I sat in the passenger seat and did not follow. Why? Because I am an Auditor-General, and an auditor knows when a ledger is closed. Mario had found a way to stop being Mario; Luigi was carrying the secret to protect the world from the fallout; and Wario was left running through empty alleyways, shouting at shadows. 
>
> I recorded the date—**18 Harvestide, 1035 BF**—closed the car door, and walked back to the tennis court. In a world where heroes vanish on farms, at least the baseline of a clay court remains 36 feet wide. WAH.

## 7. Board Findings & Eyewitness Verdict

1. **The Reality of Mario's Retirement**: Mario did not die in combat, nor was he captured by Bowser. He intentionally executed an administrative and narrative retirement on an eastern farm, leaving Luigi as the sole custodian of the secret.

4. **Waluigi's Auditor-General Objectivity**: I am the only participant in the operation who recognized that some files should remain closed. I documented the truth, released Luigi from pursuit, and returned to my clay courts.

name: The Lava-Bridge Ambush and the Blue Luigi
title: Two Hours After the Embassy: the Lava-Bridge Ambush, the Blue Luigi, and the First Cheater's Gambit
date: 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF — night, two hours after the embassy interrogation
era: The Mushroom Kingdom Regency Era (1030s BF) — Mario's Disappearance Arc
location: Bowser's Mushroom Compound (Mushroom Kingdom interior) — the gatehouse, the second-floor lava bridge, the lava lake and falls, and the calm-shore moat
