summary: Two hours after Luigi slipped out of the backseat interrogation, I tracked him to Bowser's smaller Mushroom Kingdom compound and walked into an ambush on a lava bridge. Luigi — refused by the Mages' Guild, sheltered by a Koopa — named himself Mister L, dropped the axe, and fell. A yellow-caped figure handed him a note; a Tanuki Leaf inside it flew them both toward a lava falls. Meanwhile Wario's crew kidnapped a second, smiling, blue-clad Luigi out of the Guild on forged passes, delivered him to the compound, and beat him bloody when he confessed he was Bowser's plant. The night ended with one Luigi tied up, one Luigi lost, and a three-step plan.
description: *I had already filed the embassy job as a fiasco with a body count of zero and a dignity count below that. Then the night kept going. What follows is the second half of the worst evening of my career as an auditor: a locked gate, a borrowed axe, a leaf that should not have flown that far, and two of the same man in the same compound at the same hour, one of them burnt half to the bone and the other one smiling. WAH!*
imageCaption: One object in an empty room: the axe, waiting at the far end of the bridge. I walked the whole span to reach it — and the whole span was the point.

sections.name: I. The Gate That Should Not Have Mattered
sections.overview:
Two hours after the embassy, I stood at the gate of Bowser's compound with my breath coming out white and my hands gone numb inside my gloves, staring at iron that did not care about me.

It was the smaller holding. Everyone in the car-chase business knew there was a smaller one tucked inside the Mushroom Kingdom proper, a walled annex for business Bowser did not want trucked all the way back to Darkland, and I had driven past its turnoff a dozen times without ever stopping. Now I had stopped, and the engine ticked as it cooled behind me, and the compound sat on its little volcanic blister of ground with its walls black against a sky the color of a bruise going purple.

*"Luigi... wouldn't come here."*

I said it out loud to nobody, testing the shape of it. The idea was insane on its face. Luigi hated Bowser with the particular hatred of a man who has been kidnapped-adjacent to the same villain for decades — hated him the way you hate a landlord, a tax collector, a tooth that only hurts at night. Luigi would no sooner run to Bowser's gate than I would run to Wario for a loan.

*"Right? There's no way he came here."*

But my feet did not go back to the car. That was the thing I kept coming back to, later, when the archive asked me to be precise about the hour: my feet stayed planted on the cold dirt road, and my gut kept pulling at me the way a fish pulls at a line, and the longer I stood there the more certain I became that the insane idea was the true one. This was exactly where Luigi had run. Exactly here. To the last place anyone would look, which is the first place a terrified man goes.

*WAH! I want the record to show I argued with myself for a full minute first. I am an auditor. Doubt is my whole trade. But the doubt kept losing, and the gate kept standing there, and somewhere behind that iron my idiot informant was either hiding or dying, and I have never once in my life driven away from a door like that. Ask anyone. It is my worst habit.*
sections.waluigi_note: I drove to that gate on a hunch and I will defend the hunch. Luigi had been out of my car for two hours with nowhere to go and every door in the kingdom shut to him. When a man has been refused by everyone he trusts, he goes to the one door that never pretended to love him. I knew that the way you know a song. I just did not know the song had a second verse wearing my informant's face.

sections.name: II. Three Knocks
sections.overview:
The gate stood shut. Up close it was worse than from the road: iron bars sunk into stone posts, a little security window set at head height with a shutter, and above it all a wall-walk where nobody was walking. I weighed my options the way a man weighs a coin he suspects is fake — drive away and keep hunting the backroads, or walk up to that window and announce myself to Bowser's security apparatus like a guest arriving for dinner.

My gut made the decision before my pride finished objecting.

*"Alright... fine. I'll knock."*

I crossed the dirt, planted my boots, and banged my fist on the shutter three times — *tok tok tok* — sharp enough to sting my knuckles through the glove. The sound went into the gatehouse and died there. For a long moment nothing happened, and I had time to imagine every guard on the compound mustering with spears, and then the shutter scraped back and a face appeared in the low lamplight, blinking.

*"Huh? Woah."* The guard sat up in his seat. *"What's with the getup?"*

I leaned into the window bars, squinting back, and crossed my arms in what I hoped read as menace rather than cold. *"I need to speak to Bowser."*

The guard laughed in my face. *"Ha! You really think Bowser is in THIS compound? Come on! You wouldn't last two minutes in Bowser's castle."*

*"I don't care about Bowser's castle!"* I snapped, stung exactly where the guard had aimed. Cold and tired and two hours past my dignity, I pressed my face closer to the bars. *"I need to talk to Bowser right now. It's urgent."*

*"He isn't here."* The guard leaned back, already bored. *"You won't talk to him in here..."*

*"Then where the hell is he?!"* I slammed my palm against the window frame hard enough to rattle it. *"If Bowser isn't here, then where would he be?! And why would someone run to this stupid compound if it's empty?!"*

The guard looked at me for a long moment. Then he shrugged, reached sideways without looking, and clicked a button.

*"You know what — he IS here. Second floor. Lava bridge. Take the warp pipe."*

The gate began to open.

*WAH! He gave up that fast. No bribe, no threat answered, no papers — one slammed hand and suddenly the most secure annex in the kingdom is giving out directions like a concierge. I walked through that gate and I want it understood that I KNEW it was wrong. The hinges did not even squeak. A gate that well-oiled is a gate that gets used, and used often, and nobody had told me who by.*
sections.waluigi_note: I think about that button more than any other detail of the night. Either the guard was the worst security hire in Koopa history, or the compound wanted me inside. I filed it as incompetence for years because incompetence is usually the answer. After the blue overalls came off, I refiled it. Somebody oiled those hinges, and somebody told that guard which visitors get the warp pipe.

sections.name: III. The Risers and the Axe
sections.imageCaption: The far span, and what stood on it. Risers like teeth, an axe like a signature — everything past this point was arranged.
sections.overview:
The warp pipe stood past the gate with heat shimmering off its rim. I gripped the edge — hot even through the glove — and looked down into orange dark that breathed upward at me like a sleeping animal.

*"The second floor... lava bridge?"*

I jumped.

The pipe took me the way warp pipes take everyone: all at once and with no apology. Heat climbed past me in layers, copper and sulfur and hot stone, and then I was spat out sideways onto rock that radiated warmth straight through my boots. I straightened up, blinking sweat out of my eyes, and looked around.

A narrow stone bridge spanned a lake of slow-bubbling lava. The air above it rippled. To either side the dark fell away into heat-haze and the far shore was a smear of orange, and the bridge itself ran straight and true to a far ledge where — I squinted, wiped my sleeve across my face, squinted again — where a single axe stood embedded upright in the stone, its head glinting under the flickering light.

No Bowser. No guards. No furniture, no torches, no throne, no reception committee of any kind.

Just an axe, waiting, at the far end of a bridge over lava.

*"What the hell...?"*

My mouth went dry. Every instinct I owned — auditor, athlete, survivor of Wario's business ventures — stood up at once and shouted the same thing: a room with one object in it is a room built around that object, and nobody builds a room around an axe because they ran out of chairs. I swallowed hard, suddenly and completely regretting coming here alone, unarmed, at night, on a hunch.

Behind me, from the dark at the pipe end of the bridge, somebody cleared his throat. I knew the voice before it finished the first word. I had spent the whole evening shouting at it.

*WAH! An axe. At the far end. In the stone. I have audited throne rooms, vaults, arenas, and one memorable toolshed, and I am telling you that a weapon displayed as the SOLE furnishing of a lava bridge is not decoration. It is a proposition. Somebody set that bridge the way you set a mousetrap, and the cheese was me.*
sections.waluigi_note: I never learned who set the axe there or when. It was simply there, upright in the stone, catching the light like it had been polished that morning. If the bridge was a trap built for me specifically, the trap needed two hours' notice at most — which means either astonishing logistics or somebody who knew I was coming before I did. I keep both readings on the file. Neither of them lets me sleep.

sections.name: IV. The Ambush
sections.overview:
*"You thought the Koopa worked alone?"*

I whirled. Luigi stood at the pipe end of the bridge with a Fire Flower burning in his fist and his face twisted into something I had never seen on him before — not fear, not exactly, but fear with its teeth bared. And then the fireball was already coming, straight at my chest, hissing orange-white across the gap between them.

*"LUIGI?!"*

I threw myself sideways. The fireball passed so close I felt it crisp the air by my ear — *hisssss-CRACK* as it struck the bridge behind me and burst apart in sparks that rained hissing into the lava below. I landed hard on one knee and one glove on hot stone, heart hammering against my ribs like it wanted out.

*"Crap—"*

I scrambled up, staring. Luigi stood there in the firelight with the flower pulsing in his grip and his chest heaving, and for a frozen second neither of us moved. The lava bubbled. The axe glinted. The heat pressed down like a hand.

*"You're WORKING with them?!"* My voice came out shaking between fury and something worse. *"You led me here on purpose! Were you setting this up the whole time?!"*

*"I can't believe this..."* My fists clenched so hard the gloves creaked. *"Why?! After everything we just talked about? You betrayed me?"*

I strode forward across the hot stone until only a few feet of bridge separated us, shaking all over, glowering up into the face of a man I had spent the evening screaming at and the last two hours worrying about in a way I refused to name.

*"Why would you DO this?! I trusted you! After all the time we've known each other, I never imagined you'd go this far! You know how much this hurts, right? Finding out I've been betrayed by someone I actually liked?"*

Luigi's answer came back like a slap: *"You TRUSTED me? You locked me up in your car and demanded answers!"*

*WAH! He threw a FIREBALL at me. My informant. My weeping, farm-confessing, back-door-escaping informant stood on a lava bridge and threw killing fire at my chest without a warning or a monologue first. Whatever walked out of my car two hours earlier, it was not the whole Luigi — and I say that as a man who watched him bite a Fire Flower like an apple five minutes later.*
sections.waluigi_note: Read the first line again: 'You thought the Koopa worked alone?' That is not a greeting, it is a thesis statement, and it tells me Luigi rehearsed this. Somebody — the Koopa, the Guild's shut door, the two hours of cold — convinced him that everyone he ever trusted was one organization wearing different hats. He did not ambush me as an enemy. He ambushed me as a man settling accounts with the whole world at once.

sections.name: V. The Backseat, Revisited
sections.overview:
We stood on the burning bridge and had the argument the car had not finished.

*"You think I TRUSTED you?! You kidnapped me!"* Luigi's voice cracked upward, shrill with fury. He gripped the Fire Flower until his knuckles showed white around the stem, flames licking at the air. His face was red — rage or heat or both. *"You locked me in your car like a prisoner! Threatened me! Called me a liar over and over again!"*

He thrust the flower forward. Fire curled off its petals.

*"I was just trying to find out the TRUTH!"* I shouted back, edging sideways along the bridge, eyes flicking between Luigi's face and the flame. The stone was hot through my soles. Sweat ran into my collar. *"You were the one holding all the answers! You knew where Mario was and wouldn't say a thing!"*

*"You were going to HURT me! You don't get to act like the victim here!"* Tears stood bright in Luigi's eyes, reflecting the flower's fire. *"I was scared for my life back there! And you wonder why I ran? Why I led you into a trap?"*

And then Luigi did the thing my report describes three times because I could not believe it once: he raised the Fire Flower to his mouth and bit down on it like a man biting a coin to test it. Petals crushed. Sap ran. The flower's glow surged up his throat and into his eyes, and when he spoke again his voice came layered, trembling with something bigger than anger.

*"You don't understand ANYTHING! I wasn't trying to betray you! I was trying to protect everyone from getting hurt worse than they already are!"*

I stared. Somewhere below, the lava gave a slow thick *blooop* of a bubble surfacing and bursting.

*"Send longer responses,"* the night seemed to say. Luigi obliged. What came out of him next was two hours of cold and locked doors, compressed into words.

*WAH! He BIT it. Not held, not aimed — BIT. I have been auditing this kingdom's power flora for years and I am here to tell you the Fire Flower is not produce. It is ordnance with petals. Whatever Luigi became in the next ten minutes started in his teeth, and I want that on the record before anyone calls what happened next a decision.*
sections.waluigi_note: He said 'protect everyone from getting hurt worse,' and I have turned that sentence over for years. Worse than what? Than the car? Than the farm? Than something he knew and still would not say? I accused him of holding answers in that car, and on that bridge he confirmed it — not with a confession, but with arithmetic. There was a worse. He had measured it. He still has not told me the number.

sections.name: VI. The Shut Door
sections.overview:
*"The Koopa was the only one who didn't lock me out... everyone else abandoned me."*

Luigi's voice wavered, but the words came steadier now, the way a man's words steady when he has repeated them to himself all the way somewhere. The Fire Flower's glow pulsed in his fist, throwing his shadow huge and shaking across the bridge behind him.

*"I had nowhere to go. No allies left. Not Mario, not even Peach or Luigi cared anymore."*

I listened with the lava hissing below and the heat crawling up my legs, and for the first time that night I stopped shouting. Something in the shape of the sentence — the inventory of the abandoned, recited like a ledger — got past my anger the way the fireball had gotten past my guard.

*"When I escaped the car,"* Luigi went on, *"I returned to the Mages Guild. They wouldn't let me in."*

*"They just... shut the door in my face."* His voice cracked clean open on the memory. *"After everything I'd done for them! After all my loyalty! They wouldn't even let me inside!"*

*"So I had no choice. No place left to go."* Quieter now. Bitter as ash. *"The Koopa was the only one who took me in after that. Gave me shelter when everyone else turned their backs."*

*"It's only been a few hours,"* I said — gently, for me. It was the wrong thing. I knew it was the wrong thing before the sentence finished landing.

*"Only a FEW HOURS?! You think that matters?!"* Luigi shook the flower, and sparks scattered. *"A few hours of being alone and scared is still torture! A few hours of rejection stings just as bad as days would!"*

Above us, without warning, the sky caught fire. Not the bridge, not the lake — the *sky*. Fire began raining down in streaks and gouts, and the bridge shuddered under our boots, and the lava below started churning like something down there had woken up hungry.

*WAH! 'The Koopa.' Not A koopa — THE Koopa. Definite article, capital-T in my notes. Luigi talked about this creature the way you talk about a landlord who took you in when the bank changed the locks: with the particular loyalty of a man who has exactly one creditor left. I never got a name. I never got a description. Two hours of shelter bought more allegiance than a lifetime of brotherhood, and THAT is the sentence this whole night turns on.*
sections.waluigi_note: The Guild shut its door on a man it had conscripted, and I want the Guild's apologists to sit with that before they lecture anyone about procedure. Whatever Luigi was by midnight — arsonist, victim, Mister L, all three at once — he was their man at sundown, and they locked him out into the cold with killers on every road. The Koopa opened a door. Doors are everything. Doors are the whole file.

sections.name: VII. Mister L
sections.overview:
The bridge started dying in both directions at once.

Cracks raced out from the middle with sounds like rifle shots — *CRACK-crack-CRACK* — stone splitting toward Luigi at one end and toward me at the other, chunks calving off the edges and dropping into the lava with fat spitting hisses. The fire-rain lashed down. The whole span groaned — the deep grinding voice of stressed rock — and tilted: barely, then undeniably.

*"Luigi, talk to me! What's happening?!"* I screamed over the roar, staggering back from a crack that opened between my boots. *"Why is everything burning?! Who's attacking us?!"*

Luigi answered by running for the axe.

He sprinted across the fracturing bridge with the Fire Flower abandoned somewhere behind him, chunks dropping away on either side, straight for the far ledge and the weapon standing in the stone. I watched with my stomach dropping through my boots.

*"You're trying to DESTROY the bridge?! Luigi, stop! If you cut it, we'll BOTH fall into the lava!"*

*"Luigi, what are you DOING?! If you swing that axe and cut this bridge, we're BOTH dead! Do you understand that?!"*

Luigi reached the axe. He wrapped both hands around the haft. He looked back over his shoulder through the smoke and the fire-rain, and he laughed — a short, bright, wrong little laugh that I hear still, on bad nights, underneath other sounds.

*"We're both dead?"*

He heaved the axe out of the stone. It came free with a grinding *shRIING* of rock on steel. He stood there holding it with a calm that did not belong on his face, firelight running along the blade, and he said it clearly, like a man introducing himself at a door:

*"It's Mister L now."*

*"Mister L?! What kind of stupid name is THAT?! Put the axe DOWN!"* My voice broke upward into panic. *"This isn't funny! We're both going to die if you do this!"*

And then — nothing. No swing. Luigi's face crumpled. The axe dropped out of his hands, clanged on the stone, and he went down after it, onto his knees, sobbing: huge heaving terrified sobs, clutching his own arms.

*"I-I don't know what's happening! The fire, the bridge... everything is falling apart! This wasn't supposed to happen! I didn't mean for any of this to go wrong!"*

The bridge kept dying underneath us both.

*WAH! 'It's Mister L now.' Said it like a toast. Like a christening. And then the christening lasted NINE SECONDS before the whole identity collapsed crying onto hot rock. I have seen men break and I have seen men pretend to break, and what I watched on that bridge was neither — it was a man trying on a name the way you try on a coat, finding it on fire, and tearing it off again.*
sections.waluigi_note: Nine seconds. I counted them later against the bridge sounds and I stand by the count: nine seconds of Mister L, and then Luigi again, weeping. Whatever that name is — armor, alias, symptom, summons — it did not survive contact with its first crisis. Remember that the next time the Regency waves a warrant with that letter on it. I watched the name get born and I watched it fail, and both happened before the bridge finished falling.

sections.name: VIII. The Yellow Cape
sections.imageCaption: Nine words, flatly placed — and a cape the color of a warning. The courier never raised its voice. It never had to.
sections.overview:
The shaking started before the figure appeared — a deep judder that ran the length of the dying bridge and set my teeth rattling. Smoke boiled up off the lava in thick banks, and through it came a shape: tall, caped, silent, with a yellow cape hanging behind its back like a flag from a country nobody had declared yet.

*"Wh— who's THERE?!"* I spun, nearly losing my footing on the cracked stone. *"Who the hell are you?! Show yourself!"*

The figure did not answer. It moved the way smoke moves — no hurry, no wasted motion — and reached Luigi where he knelt sobbing by the dropped axe. And then it *spun*, cape flaring out in a full whipping circle, and the edge of that yellow cloth caught Luigi square and sent him flying sideways across the bridge like a thrown doll.

*"LUIGI!"*

Luigi fetched up at the very edge of the span, half over the drop, staring up. The figure stood over him, faceless in the smoke, and extended one hand. In it: [[prop:prop_cape_note_still_unread|a folded note]].

*"Luigi... read it. Read the note."* The voice was flat and mechanical, eerie in its calm, each word placed like a tile. *"This changes everything."*

Luigi took the paper with shaking hands. The figure held still one beat longer — long enough for me to understand, with cold certainty, that it knew exactly where I was standing and had chosen not to care — and then it ran: off across the collapsing bridge, gone into the smoke between one breath and the next, cape and all, as if it had never needed the bridge to hold it.

The slab Luigi knelt on gave a sharp *CRACK* and began to tip toward the lava.

*WAH! Read that sequence back and tell me it parses as anything but a delivery. The shaking announces the courier. The courier demonstrates — on Luigi's body, at speed — that resistance is comedy. The goods change hands: one folded note, contents unverified to this day. The courier exits stage smoke. I have received registered post with less ceremony and more paperwork than that ghost gave my informant.*
sections.waluigi_note: I never saw its face, never heard a name, never found a witness who admits to hiring it. Two sentences spoken, nine words total, and the yellow cape is the whole description and I have spent years showing that description to people who know things. Nobody claims it. But somebody wrote a note, somebody folded a Tanuki Leaf inside it, and somebody paid a courier that walks collapsing bridges like sidewalks. That is three somebodies, minimum, and the file holds zero of them.

sections.name: IX. The Best Friend
sections.overview:
I did not hesitate. I lunged across the breaking bridge with my arm outstretched, stone crumbling under my boots, reaching for Luigi as the slab under Luigi gave way —

I missed. My fingers closed on hot empty air, and Luigi went down through the wreckage with the note clutched to his chest, and then the whole middle of the bridge went with a roar like the world clearing its throat, and I was falling too, into smoke so thick I could not see my own gloves.

*"LUIGI! NO! This can't be happening... THIS CAN'T BE HAPPENING!"*

I fell through choking grey that burned going down, coughing hard enough to double over mid-air, screaming Luigi's name into it until my voice shredded. The fall ended the way falls end in that compound: not on rock, but *in* the lake system — I came down sprawling on a slab of floating debris riding the slow lava current, gasping, half-blind, alive.

*"Luigi! Can you hear me?! Say something! Please... if you're alive, talk to me!"*

Nothing. Only the crawl of the current and the pop of the lava and my own coughing. Then, through a tear in the smoke: a shoe. Luigi's shoe, sitting upright on a nearby rock as if its owner had just stepped out of it. And beyond it, on another rock, the folded note — smoke-darkened, intact — riding the same slow current toward the distant thunder that I now understood, with sinking horror, was a waterfall. Of lava. Of course it was a waterfall. Of course it was lava.

*"Luigi! The note! Grab onto that rock, whatever you can!"*

My own slab rocked. A hand came up over its edge — a white glove, scorched grey at the fingers — and gripped. The slab tilted. I froze, staring down as the glove hauled and a head rose into view: a face half-charred black, blistered and raw down one side, the mustache singed to a ruin.

The ruined mouth moved. The voice came out thin as paper.

*"Its a-me. Your best friend."*

*"...Luigi? Luigi, it's really you?"* My own voice cracked in half. *"Oh my god... what happened to you?! How are you even alive after falling like that?!"*

Luigi did not answer. He hauled himself fully onto the slab, staggered upright, and jumped — clean across open lava — to the rock with the note, and snatched it up.

*WAH! 'Its a-me. Your best friend.' Said with HALF A FACE. I have been threatened by warlords, sued by Wario, and audited by my own reflection, and nothing in my life has ever landed the way those five words landed, wheezed through burnt lips on a rock in a river of fire. If that was acting, strike my name from the auditors' roll, because I cannot tell the difference and I no longer want to.*
sections.waluigi_note: The shoe bothers me more than the face. The face I understand — fire does what fire does. But the shoe was sitting UPRIGHT. Upright, on its own rock, as if placed. Either the current has a stage manager's instincts, or somebody in that smoke arranged the scene before I arrived. I filed the shoe as debris. I think about it as staging. The file and I disagree, and the file is winning on points.

sections.name: X. The Leaf
sections.overview:
Luigi unfolded the note with burnt fingers, and something slipped out of the fold into his palm: a Tanuki Leaf, golden-brown, whole, shimmering faintly in the firelight like a coin at the bottom of a fountain.

*"Luigi... what's that? Where did you get that? What does it say?"*

Luigi did not look up. He pressed the leaf flat — and the change took him the way a struck match takes: all at once. Fur, ears, tail, the whole tanuki rig blooming out of a half-burnt man on a rock in a lava lake, and then he was sprinting, full tilt across the floating debris, leaping rock to rock with the waterfall thundering closer ahead.

*"Wh— wait, what?! What are you doing?! Luigi, STOP! Where are you going?!"*

I ran after him, boots skidding on hot rock, jumping gaps I could not see the bottoms of, and caught up only when Luigi did the worst thing yet: spread his arms and *flew*. Up off the debris field, wobbling, climbing into the smoke with the waterfall's roar swelling under him like an orchestra tuning for a finale.

*"Luigi! Slow down! Wait! Give me your hand! You're going to crash into something if you keep going like this! Land somewhere SAFE!"*

No answer. I judged the wobble, timed the dip, and jumped — fingers closing around Luigi's ankle mid-air, hauling down with all my weight. They dropped together back toward the rocks.

*"Got you! You idiot! You could've gotten yourself killed flying like that near the lava waterfall!"* I locked both hands around the ankle and held on while Luigi kicked. *"You reckless idiot! What were you thinking?! If I hadn't grabbed you, you would've crashed into something or flown right off a cliff!"*

That was when my phone rang.

*"Oh, come ON, seriously?! Who even calls right now?!"* I fished it out one-handed, still gripping the kicking ankle, and stared at the screen. *"Wario? What the hell does he want right now? Ugh... I swear if this is about Mario again..."*

I answered. It was about Mario. It was also about Luigi. It was, I would reflect later, about a Luigi currently dangling over lava by one ankle versus a Luigi currently standing next to Wario being extremely helpful — and the impossibility of both statements landed on me at exactly the same moment, over open lava, holding a phone in one hand and a flying burn victim in the other.

sections.name: XI. The Falls
sections.overview:
Wario's voice on the phone was triumphant: *"We found Luigi! Get your butt over here before Wario shows him the true Wario style!"*

*"What? You FOUND Luigi?! But he's RIGHT HERE with me! Are you talking about another Luigi? Because this one is literally dangling over lava right now!"*

*"How can that be him when he is standing right HERE? Come on, let me put-a him on the phone—"*

And then a voice came through the speaker that stopped my blood: Luigi's voice. Unmistakably. Cheerful. Unhurt. Talking on Wario's phone while the burnt original kicked weakly at the end of my arm.

*"Huh? That... that can't be real. That's impossible."*

The rocks were visibly accelerating toward the falls. Wario came back on, talking fast: *"Hey, so here's the deal — Luigi was hiding at the Mages Guild. We got [[prop:prop_forged_guild_pass_compound|fake passes]], went in, and kidnapped him."*

*"Hold up. Slow down. You're saying you faked passes and infiltrated the Mages Guild? And kidnapped Luigi? But I'm HOLDING him right now!"*

*"Then who is—"* the line crackled, died, and left me shouting into static: *"Hey! Hello?! Answer me! Damn it... who were we even talking to?"*

The lava sounds were louder now — a continuous bass roar with the falls' white-orange curtain visible through the smoke ahead, close enough that spray stung my face. And Luigi, at the end of my arm, had gone limp. Shallow breathing. Unstable. Gone under.

*"Luigi... come on, stay with me! Wake up! PLEASE wake up! I can't lose you like this!"* I shook him, shouted, shook him again. The roar swallowed everything. *"This isn't happening... we can't die like this! Not here, not now!"*

*"Huh?"*

Luigi's eyes fluttered open. At the same instant their rock hit faster water and tilted violently, slamming sideways into another slab with a jolt that nearly threw us both clear.

*"Luigi! You're awake! The rock's tilting — hold on TIGHT!"*

Then the current took Luigi's slab and *tore* it sideways — Luigi went flying off our shared rock onto a separate one already moving faster than anything I could match, shrinking into the smoke toward the light at the falls' lip. Too far. Too fast. A jump now was suicide for both of us, and I stood on my own tilting rock with the decision ripping me in half for one eternal second.

*"I'm sorry, Luigi! If I try, we'll both get swept away! I have to... stay here."*

The current took me — spat me out the side channel onto a calm lava shore, the moat outside the compound walls, ground level, solid dirt under my boots. No Luigi. No rock. No note. Just the compound looming ahead and the moat lapping quiet orange at my feet.

*"Luigi... where are you? That idiot got swept away! He could be dead for all I know!"* I kicked a rock hard enough to hurt my own foot. *"Where the hell did you go?! This can't be happening... I just lost him! After everything!"*

The phone rang again.

*WAH! I let go. I want that written plainly where nobody can soften it later: I looked at the gap, I did the arithmetic, and I let my informant go over a lava falls rather than follow him into it. Every auditor in this building can tell you the arithmetic was correct. None of them has ever had to stand on the shore afterward shouting a dead man's name at a moat. The arithmetic does not cover that part.*
sections.waluigi_note: Two things I need on this record. First: the tanuki flight ended BEFORE the falls — Luigi was limp and powerless when the current took him, which means whatever the leaf gave him, it spent itself on the sprint. Second: I never saw him go over. I saw him carried toward the light and then I was spat out sideways and he was gone. Missing is not dead. The file says missing. I say it louder every year.

sections.name: XII. The Blue Luigi
sections.imageCaption: What the Blue Luigi left behind: blue overalls, empty, grinning with nobody inside. The costume came away like a husk.
sections.overview:
I snatched the phone up. *"Damn it, this AGAIN?! What?!"*

Wario's voice, panicked through static: the Luigi they had — *"Listen. The Luigi we had... he told us where Mario was. We are on our way there."*

*"You found Mario?! Where are you headed? What did Luigi tell you?!"*

*"He said he was near Bowser's compound"* — the one I was standing outside of, soaked, burnt, and alone — *"anyway, time is money, we are headed over there."*

*"Wait... what? The Luigi I just saw was burned and barely conscious! How could he have told you anything useful?! Unless..."* The thought arrived fully formed and freezing cold. *"Wario, listen to me carefully. The Luigi I just had was half-dead and couldn't even talk. There's no way he gave you Mario's location. Someone is LYING."*

Then Mona was on the line instead, voice thin through the crackle, trying audibly not to panic. *"Waluigi... we need to talk. We found Mario... but something is very wrong. The Luigi we're with... he's not acting like himself. He gave us Mario's location too easily. It feels off."*

*"What do you mean, not acting like himself? Did he say anything weird? Or move strangely?"* My mind was already racing down the list — clone, duplicate, impostor, worse. *"Mona, where are you guys right now? Are you close to Mario yet?"*

*"Mona, hold on a second—"*

Headlights. Above the moat, on the compound road: Wario's car, rolling in with its brights on. And in it — I nearly dropped the phone into the lava — Luigi. Standing-height, blue-clad, perfectly healthy, *waving*. Taller somehow. Cheerful. Nothing out of place except everything.

*"What the hell...?!"*

The car crunched to a stop at the gate with Wario driving and Mona, Ashley, and Jimmy T crammed in around the waving figure. They talked to the guard. And then the blue Luigi strolled up to the window himself, smiled one slow smile — and the guard opened the gate. Just like that. No button drama, no shouting, no two-minute hazing. The smile was sufficient.

*"They're letting them in? Just like that?"* I ducked lower behind the moat rocks, watching the car roll through. For one split second the blue figure turned its head toward my hiding place. The face didn't move right. Too stiff. Too calm. A smile like paint.

Then they were inside, and the gate was shut, and I was alone again with the moat and the wrongness of it crawling up my spine.

*"That smile... that wasn't Luigi. That was something else."*

I dialed Wario back with shaking fingers. *"Wario, what did you just let inside?! That wasn't Luigi! That thing smiled like a creepy robot — why would security just open up for it?!"*

*"Huh? What do you—"*

The bang cut him off. A deep concussive *BOOM* from inside the compound, shaking dust off the moat rocks — and right on its heels, wailing into the night: Wario's car alarm.

*"What the hell was that explosion?! They triggered an alarm! That thing with Wario did something wrong!"*

The entrance wall burst outward in a shower of rubble and dust. And through the wreckage, unhurried, humming, walked the blue Luigi — untouched, unbothered, smiling that same empty painted smile. He stopped in the open, still humming his little tune, and began peeling off the blue overalls. Underneath: the familiar green shirt and jeans. The costume came away like a husk.

*"You really are an idiot,"* he said pleasantly, to everyone and no one. *"All of you."*

*WAH! The gate opened for a SMILE. I banged on that window until my hand rang and got interrogated about my outfit; this thing strolled up, showed its teeth, and the iron swung wide like it was EXPECTED. Either that guard runs the most corrupt checkpoint in the kingdom or the compound knew its own asset on sight. I filed both readings. I believe the second one the way I believe in gravity.*
sections.waluigi_note: Mona's phone call is the bravest record of the night and I want her credited: while riding in a car with the thing, she told me it was wrong. 'Too easily' — those were her words about Mario's location, and they are the exact tell every auditor is trained to hear. Intelligence that arrives too easily is not intelligence. It is bait. She knew it at speed, in the dark, with the bait sitting next to her.

sections.name: XIII. The Confession
sections.overview:
What followed, in the dust of the burst wall, was the longest confession I have ever heard delivered as comedy.

*"Wow! You guys really fell for it, huh? I mean... seriously? Wario didn't even question me once!"* The thing giggled — light, musical, wrong in a way that raised the hairs on my arms. *"And Mona! Ashley! Jimmy T! Oh man, you all just handed Wario right to Bowser on a silver platter."*

It tilted its head. The smile never moved.

*"It was simple, my plan, really. After I saw you all running like headless chickens I thought I would help you find Luigi and Mario. Get your happy ending."* Another giggle, high and joyless. *"My plan worked perfectly. You all ran around like idiots chasing clues while Bowser got exactly what he wanted."*

On and on it went, pacing the rubble, twirling its own hair, savoring each name: Wario's excitement, Mona's gratitude, Ashley upset, Jimmy T silent. *"You really thought Bowser wouldn't have spies? That he wouldn't send someone in disguised as one of you? You guys are WAY too trusting."* From inside the compound came shouting — panicked, multiplying — and the thing clapped its hands in delight. *"Ohhh, and now the screaming starts! I can hear Wario yelling! Hahaha!"*

It never noticed the car starting. Wario, out of the wreckage and behind the wheel with murder in his eyes, reversed straight into it — *THUMP* — and the confession ended mid-giggle with the impostor sprawled in the dust clutching its shoulder.

*"OW!! What is wrong with you?! You could've killed me!!"*

*"I COULD'VE killed you?"* Wario was already climbing out, knuckles cracking like popcorn. *"YOU could have killed ME!"*

*WAH! Listen to the giggle and tell me that is a person. A person laughs because something is funny. That thing laughed the way a music box plays — same notes, same tempo, no matter what room it is in. It giggled describing its own plan, giggled at screaming it caused, giggled with blood on its lip later. The laugh was part of the costume, same as the overalls, and it came off about as easily.*
sections.waluigi_note: The confession is tradecraft wearing a clown nose and I want the file to treat it as evidence, not entertainment. Note what it admits: Bowser runs spies in friendly faces, the Mario lead was bait, and the crew was herded, not hunted. Note what it never says: a name, a handler, a price. It told us everything about the operation and nothing about the operator. That is not bragging. That is a cover story with the serial numbers performing.

sections.name: XIV. The Reckoning
sections.overview:
The fight was short, ugly, and six-against-one. Wario led with a haymaker the impostor ducked, taunting — *"Slow as hell! Is this all you've got?"* — until I charged in and it got worse for the fraud from there. Mona and Jimmy T piled out of the car. Ashley stepped forward with her face like winter and said nothing at all, which frightened the impostor more than the shouting had.

Then Wario's fist connected with a sickening *CRACK* that wiped the smile off for one beautiful half-second. Ashley raised her witch's broom — *"What the—?! A witches broom?!"* — and the interrogation began in earnest: Wario with a fistful of collar (*"Who sent you?! What's your real name?!"*), Ashley with the broom cocked, Mona twisting one arm behind its back, Jimmy T taking the other.

That was when I did the thing the bards will not shut up about. I stepped forward, pointed one long finger at the thing wearing my informant's face, and shouted with all the fury of the bridge, the falls, the moat, and the lost shoe:

*"YOU CHEATED!"*

The first Cheater's Gambit. Ever deployed. The crew took it up like a war cry — *"Yeah, you CHEATED!"* — and the reckoning rolled on: a Wario headbutt (*CRUNCH*, blood from the nose), Ashley's broom coming down across its back with a magical *WHAM*, both arms pinned, five furious faces closing in.

*"You gonna talk now, or are we gonna have to beat the truth out of you?! We're waiting."*

*"I'm NOT telling you anything! Go ahead! Hit me all you want! I don't care!"*

Ashley mounted her broom. The impostor took one look up at her, hovering, and its whole performance shattered into raw panic: *"Wha— NO! Let me GO!"*

*"You have ONE last chance,"* Ashley said coldly from above. *"Tell us who you are and why you impersonated Luigi."*

*"I-I'm not saying anything!"*

Ashley reached down, took a fistful of its shirt, and lifted. What happened on that ride is attested only by its ending: one hour later, outside the compound walls, the impostor lay unconscious, tied hand and foot, out of smiles at last.

*WAH! 'YOU CHEATED!' I said it and I meant it and I would say it again in front of any tribunal in any kingdom. That thing did not beat us. It did not outfight us or outthink us. It marked the cards, stacked the deck, and dealt itself my friend's face — and there is exactly one auditor's answer to a marked deck, which is to name it OUT LOUD. The Gambit was born on a pile of rubble at midnight and it has never once been deployed against an honest opponent since.*
sections.waluigi_note: The crew's discipline in that brawl deserves the file's respect: five people, one fraud, and nobody killed it. Wario wanted to. I wanted to. Ashley could have. Instead we took it alive, took it apart verbally, and took it for a ride — because a dead spy is a rumor and a live one is a door. Every interrogation I have run since starts from that rubble: keep the asset breathing, take the arms first, and let the quietest person in the room ask the last question.

sections.name: XV. Three Steps
sections.overview:
One hour later, outside the compound, the group stood around in the cold with an unconscious prisoner and a problem nobody wanted to say first.

*"That idiot really thought he could just get away with lying to us?!"* Wario huffed, arms crossed. Mona rubbed her temples. Jimmy T kicked a rock hard enough to skitter it off the wall. And I told them — finally, fully — about the other Luigi: the ambush, the axe, the yellow cape, the note, the leaf, the falls. The burns. The shoe sitting upright on its rock. The hand letting go.

*"That Luigi I saved from falling into the lava... he was barely alive. He couldn't talk, could barely move. He had burns everywhere and looked half-dead. There's no way that guy could've been lying to us or tricking anyone."*

*"So... there were two Luigis?"* Mona said slowly. *"One real and one fake?"*

*"And then THAT thing showed up with Wario, acting all cheerful and normal!"* I jabbed a finger at the tied bundle. *"That thing didn't even look scared when the compound exploded! The real Luigi would've been freaking out!"*

*"The real one was probably still hurt somewhere... while this impostor tricked us."* Ashley nodded, eyes on the prisoner.

*"So where the hell is the REAL Luigi now?!"* Wario exploded, pacing. *"If that fake one was with us this whole time... then what happened to the REAL one?! Was he captured?! Did Bowser take him somewhere else?!"*

*"We need to find the real Luigi!"* Pacing, shouting, more pacing. *"We have to split up—"*

*"Splitting up got us into this mess in the first place,"* Mona said quietly, and the whole group went still, because she was right and everyone knew it. Wario deflated mid-stride. *"Well then how the hell are we gonna find him?! We don't even know where to start! The real Luigi could be anywhere in this damn place!"*

*"I have an idea."*

I held up one finger. The crew turned to look at me — Wario mid-fume, Mona hopeful, Ashley already gripping her broom like step one, Jimmy T with one eyebrow raised.

*"Step one: we interrogate this fake Luigi properly. Find out who sent him and why."*

*"Step two: we check the security footage from Bowser's compound. If that fake came in with Wario earlier... maybe they filmed something useful."*

Mona's eyes lit up. Ashley nodded slowly. Jimmy T finally spoke: *"And step three?"*

*"Step THREE... we start checking the rest of the compound ourselves. Every room, every hall, every nook and cranny. We find our way through this damn place and don't leave until we've searched it all."*

Mona's eyes shone. Ashley smiled — a small cold thing, but a smile. Jimmy T grinned slyly. Wario cracked his knuckles like a man accepting a contract. Then I held out my palm, and Wario — for once in his life, without argument — fished the forged Guild pass from his pocket and slapped it into the glove: souvenir of the infiltration, evidence of the felony, and the only paper the night produced that anyone was allowed to read.

Behind them, in the rubble of the burst wall, the blue overalls lay where the impostor had tossed them: empty, bright, grinning with nobody inside.

*WAH! Three steps. Interrogate, investigate, invade — in that order, no splitting up, no more hunches at midnight. It is the most professional plan I have ever issued and I issued it soaked to the bone with lava in my boots. And the overalls are still there, in the rubble, as far as the file knows. Empty blue. Nobody inside. If that is not this whole night folded into one object, I do not know what is.*
sections.waluigi_note: I filed the plan and I stand by the plan, but the file should show what the plan assumes: that the real Luigi is findable, that the impostor is breakable, and that the compound's cameras saw anything worth seeing. All three assumptions have failed me before. Still — three steps beats no steps, and 'don't split up' is the first lesson this crew ever learned the expensive way. We paid for it in burns. We intend to keep it.

participants.name: Waluigi
participants.role: Tracked Luigi to the compound on a hunch; knocked, descended, got ambushed; lost Luigi at the falls; named the fraud aloud with the first Cheater's Gambit; issued the three-step plan

participants.name: Luigi
participants.role: Ambushed Waluigi on the lava bridge with a Fire Flower; told the shut-door story; became Mister L for nine seconds; took the caped figure's note; flew the Tanuki Leaf; went over the falls' edge and is missing

participants.name: Wario
participants.role: Kidnapped the blue Luigi out of the Mages' Guild on forged passes; drove him to the compound; reversed the car into him on reveal; headbutted him; demanded the search for the real one

participants.name: Mona
participants.role: Rode the Guild job; warned Waluigi by phone that their Luigi was wrong; held the impostor's arm through the reckoning

participants.name: Ashley
participants.role: 'We trusted you.' Worked the impostor with her broom, gave the last chance from above, and took him for the ride that ended him conscious-free and tied

participants.name: Jimmy T
participants.role: Rode the Guild job; held the impostor's second arm; asked for step three and grinned at the answer

outcome:
The impostor is captured — beaten, broomed, unconscious, and tied outside the compound walls, still nameless. The real Luigi is missing past the lava falls with severe burns and an unread note. The yellow-caped figure is unidentified and at large. Mario's location (near the compound, via the impostor's bait) is unverified. The crew holds together under my three-step plan: interrogate, pull the footage, search the compound.

Sequel status: The Garden Above the Fire completes the third step of the plan — the compound search — by finding Luigi alive, recovering his remembered line from the note, and moving the open lead from the falls to the garden above the fire.
notableFeatures: The nine seconds of Mister L — the name spoken aloud on the bridge, then dropped with the axe
A yellow-caped courier who walks collapsing bridges, speaks seven words, and delivers one note
The note that has never been read — and the Tanuki Leaf folded inside it
Luigi's shoe, sitting upright on its own rock in the lava lake
Two Luigis in one compound: one burnt half to the bone, one smiling in blue
The gate that opened for a smile after refusing Waluigi's knocking
The first Cheater's Gambit, deployed at midnight on a pile of rubble
Ashley's broom ride — the interrogation's last chance, taken
Sequel hook resolved: Luigi is later found alive in the lava-moat tunnel system and carried to Dr. Toad's Star Hill clinic.

keyBattles.name: The Impostor's Reckoning
keyBattles.description: Six against one in the rubble of the burst entrance wall: Wario reverses the car into the revealed impostor, then wades in swinging; Waluigi joins; Mona and Jimmy T pin the arms; Ashley works the enchanted broom and delivers the last chance from above. No weapons drawn on the crew's side beyond the broom and the car; no surrender offered on the impostor's.
keyBattles.outcome: Impostor beaten bloody, unmasked, and — after Ashley's ride — unconscious and tied. No deaths. No names given.

aftermath: The compound keeps its breached entrance wall and its missing bridge; nobody has filed a repair order, and Bowser's office has said nothing about the night at all. The impostor sits bound outside the walls with five witnesses to everything except his name. The real Luigi was owed a search of the falls' outflow and the moat system — the three-step plan's third step — and that sequel search is now filed: Luigi survived long enough to be found in the volcanic tunnels and carried to treatment. The caped figure's note remains unread, its contents known only to a missing burn victim. The Mages' Guild has not acknowledged the forged passes, the abduction from its halls, or the shut door that started it. My boots still smell of sulfur.
waluigiAssessment: 1. The night had two operations, not one. Luigi's ambush was desperation with a borrowed axe; the impostor's helpfulness was tradecraft with a rehearsed smile. They share a compound and an hour but not a commander — unless the commander is Bowser running both sides of the board, which the file cannot prove and I cannot stop suspecting. 2. Mister L lasted nine seconds. Whatever that name becomes later — warrant, warning, wardrobe — it began as a drowning man's last grab at agency, and the archive should never let the Regency pretend otherwise. 3. The note is the most important unread document in this building. A courier that capable does not deliver trivia, and the Tanuki Leaf inside was transport, not message — which means the message is still in play, in the pocket of a missing man. 4. Mona was right first and Ashley finished it. The crew's instincts outperformed its leadership all night; Wario drove the fraud to the door and I walked into the trap, and the women in the car are the reason anyone has a prisoner instead of a crater. 5. Recommendation: run the three steps in order, starting with the prisoner before Bowser's people come back for him — because a smile that opens gates is an asset, and assets get retrieved. 6. Addendum after the sequel: the recommendation was correct. The prisoner led to the right search path, Luigi lived, and the note finally gained a remembered sentence. That does not make the prisoner trustworthy. It makes the next door legible.

description: *The plan had three steps: interrogate, pull the footage, search the compound. We got as far as step one before step three ran bleeding out of the dark. This is the sequel to the lava-bridge file and the close of that arc: one prisoner talking too easily, two ninja witnesses who should not have been there, one burned Luigi asking a question meant for someone else, and one clinic where the word brother hurt worse than the bandages. WAH.*

sections.name: I. Water on the Wrong Luigi
sections.overview:
Mona poured the water with the expression of a person who had decided mercy and irritation could use the same bottle. It hit the fake Luigi in the face and ran under his green cap, and he came up coughing against the rope with the whole crew standing over him. Wario loomed first. Wario always looms first when the room needs a wall with a mustache.

*"Wake up. Now."*

The impostor blinked at Wario, then at Mona, then at Ashley's broom. Jimmy T cracked his knuckles once, a small dry sound in the scorched air outside the compound. I had my pen out. I do not know when I had taken it out. There are nights when the hand reaches for a weapon and nights when the hand reaches for a record. This was both.

Mona planted both hands on her hips. *"You've got some explaining to do."*

He tried to sit up, winced, and discovered the knot. The bravado went out of his face one feature at a time: smile first, chin second, eyes last. He was still wearing enough of Luigi to make the sight insulting. Blue cloth lay in the rubble behind him from the reveal, empty and bright like a joke nobody had survived.

*"Alright, alright... I get it,"* he said. *"I'll talk."*

*WAH! Prisoners who agree too quickly are either broken or beginning the next lie. I marked both readings before he reached the second sentence. That is not cynicism. That is craft learned in Wario's accounting office.*
sections.waluigi_note: The first plan did exactly what it was supposed to do: wake the false Luigi, keep him outnumbered, and make him spend words. Wario wanted to hit him again. Ashley wanted the broom ready. Mona wanted answers. I wanted one sentence he could not have learned from smiling at Wario in a car. We got more than one. That was not automatically good news.

sections.name: II. The Brothers in the Hall
sections.overview:
The impostor said the fight had happened before Bowser sent him to us. Mario and Luigi, in the castle halls, screaming loud enough for enemies to stop pretending not to listen.

*"You thought Koopa worked alone,"* he said, and my stomach turned because I had heard Luigi throw that line at me on the bridge.

Then he gave us pieces. Not clean testimony; nobody recalls a brother breaking in clean lines. He remembered Mario pleading through it — *"Luigi, what do you mean by that? I have fought-a far too much, and you stand against me... you're my brother, that's not something that'll go away."* He remembered Luigi spitting back that being a brother meant little when the world used him as a step. He remembered them talking over each other until the words stopped sounding like sentences and started sounding like furniture breaking in another room.

Mario tried to say the memories mattered. Luigi answered that something inside him had already been paid for in neglect. Then came the line that made Mona put a hand over her mouth and made Ashley's broom drop half an inch.

*"You were never my brother."*

The impostor looked down when he said it, which is the first human thing I had seen him do. He claimed both of them were crying near the end. He claimed Mario still tried to reach through the masquerade, still said Koopa had made Luigi insane and that he could relieve the pain. He claimed Luigi pushed him away anyway.

Wario did not interrupt. Wario, who interrupts weather, debt collectors, and occasionally gravity, stood silent while the rope creaked around the prisoner.

*WAH! I do not trust tears reported by a spy. I trust a phrase repeated in the wrong mouth, because phrases leave fingerprints. The bridge gave us 'Koopa worked alone.' The prisoner gave it back with a hallway around it.*
sections.waluigi_note: The argument is not filed here as truth in every word. It is filed as a witness statement from a compromised source, backed by one phrase Luigi had already said where the impostor was not supposed to have heard it unless the hallway story had a real spine. That is enough to pursue. It is not enough to forgive anyone.

sections.name: III. Yellow Cape, East Passage
sections.overview:
I asked about the yellow-caped figure because the file had started to revolve around that color. The impostor's head came up too fast.

*"A yellow cape, you say?"*

He had seen someone leaving the castle. He had seen them give Luigi something. He pointed east, toward the passage under the compound where the heat breathed out in pulses. Wario grabbed my arm before I could run.

*"You really believe this guy?"*

I tried to tear free. *"That yellow cape handed Luigi a note today. That is important!"*

Wario shook me once, hard enough to make my teeth click. *"He tricked us. He could be feeding us Bowser's next trap."*

He was not wrong. That was the worst part. He almost never is when he is being annoying at close range. But the phrase had already done its work in my head. Luigi had used it on the bridge. The fake knew it. Bowser had overheard the fight, or the spy had, or both. Either way, the prisoner was not improvising from nothing.

*"Besides,"* I said, breath scraping, *"how would he know Luigi was working for the Koopa?"*

That stopped Wario better than strength did. Mona stepped in with her voice low and urgent, saying we could not ignore the lead. Ashley nodded, eyes narrowed toward the tunnel. Jimmy T muttered something that sounded like a curse doing stretches.

Wario let go.

*"Let's find Luigi,"* he said.

We did not thank the prisoner. We did not untie him. We ran.
sections.waluigi_note: The decision point matters. The party did not trust the impostor; the party trusted the overlap between his story and facts already heard in blood, smoke, and falling stone. That is the difference between gullibility and investigation. Wario will deny I made that distinction out loud because it makes me sound reasonable.

sections.name: IV. The Moat Witnesses
sections.overview:
We chose the lava moat before the east passage swallowed the whole night. I had last seen Luigi near the falls. If he was hurt, the waterless river of fire would have carried him somewhere, and if he was dead I did not want the prisoner choosing where I learned it.

The heat hit us in the face before the glow did. Lava fell in sheets, orange and white, throwing light against black stone. Wario shouted Luigi's name over the roar until the word broke apart. Mona cupped her hands and called too. Ashley flew higher, because witches are useful in exactly the ways tall men hate admitting.

From above, Ashley saw smoke and two shapes. Kat and Ana stood on the high rocks, small against the glow, waving like this was the least convenient rooftop in the kingdom.

*"What are you two doing here?"* Wario bellowed.

They had followed us. Of course they had followed us. They were not part of the mission. They had no business near a lava moat. They were our friends, which is the most dangerous kind of credential because nobody stamps it and everybody obeys it. Wario yelled anyway. Mona rubbed her temples. I saved my breath because the next question mattered more.

*"Did you see Luigi?"*

Kat shouted yes. Ana shouted that he was limping but alive. Burns on his arms and legs. Exhausted. Face not burned.

I did not realize I had been holding my breath until Ana said his face was fine. It left me all at once, hot and ugly. Then came the part that made the note feel colder than the lava. Luigi had not said much. He had kept repeating two words.

*"Find them."*

*WAH! WarioWare loyalty is a medical condition. Kat and Ana caught it early and brought it to the lava moat. I should reprimand them. I am filing their witness statements instead, which is how the archive admits gratitude without making it a habit.*
sections.waluigi_note: Kat and Ana were not supposed to be there, but their sighting saved the search. The detail that Luigi's face was unburned is not cosmetic. It told us he had been shielded from the worst of the fall, turned away from the heat, or lucky in a way that deserves its own shrine and a tax form.

sections.name: V. The Green Cap in the Tunnel
sections.imageCaption: After the fire: clean bandages, a soot-smudged green cap, and the folded sentence that turned the whole night toward the next arc.
sections.overview:
Kat pointed. Ana ran. Jimmy T yelled *"wait up"* while hopping the safer rocks, which were safer only by the standard of not being actively molten. Mona grabbed his hand and dragged him through the last stretch. Ashley circled back, then shot ahead. Wario and I ran like the tunnel owed us money.

Then I saw the cap.

Green, familiar, slumped against the cavern wall above a smear of smoke. Luigi sat under it with his back to the stone, burned arms wrapped in strips torn from his own shirt, sweat shining on a face gone pale from heat and pain. He was conscious. Not well. Conscious. His lips moved before we reached him.

*"Are we-a still superstars?"*

Wario dropped beside him. Mona touched his arm and Luigi flinched away so violently that the whole group froze.

*"Don't-a touch me..."*

His eyes opened, glassy and unfocused. *"M-Mario?"*

The name cracked in the middle. Wario leaned in with the least gentle bedside manner ever issued to a rescue. *"It's not Mario, idiot. It's Wario."*

Luigi blinked until he found me. Relief crossed his face so nakedly I looked away from it.

*"W-Waluigi... You... you came for me."*

I crouched before my knees could ask permission. The question came out sharper than I meant it. *"Luigi, what did that letter say? Please tell me."*

He coughed and let Wario brace him upright. The words came slowly, each one dragged over broken glass.

*"The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire."*

That was the reading. Not the paper — the paper was gone, still unrecovered — but the first text of [[prop:prop_courier_note_garden_above_fire|the courier's note]] ever spoken into the archive. Luigi did not understand it. He only knew someone had handed it to him before everything fell apart.
sections.waluigi_note: This is the hinge. Previous filing: unread note, missing reader. This filing: living reader, remembered text, still no paper. The phrase is too neat to be a direction and too useful to be poetry. Garden above the fire is where the next search begins, but do not let the romance of a clue erase the fact that it arrived after a brother was broken open by someone who knew exactly where to hand it to him.

sections.name: VI. Still Superstars
sections.overview:
Luigi's eyes drifted past us, past the tunnel, past every face that had run itself ragged to reach him. He was not speaking to the group. He was not speaking to himself. He was speaking to someone absent, and the absence filled the cavern more completely than Bowser's lava ever could.

*"We are still superstars, right?"*

Nobody answered because the wrong person was supposed to answer. The lava bubbled below us, slow and bright. Mona's hand hovered near Luigi's unburned arm and stopped there, not touching. Ashley sat beside him anyway, quiet as a candle. Jimmy T looked down at his shoes. Wario turned his face away first.

I should have said something clever. I am excellent at clever. Clever is armor with polish on it. Instead my throat closed until every word had to climb out.

*"Luigi... focus on us. Talk to me."*

He did not. He whispered it again, smaller. *"Are we still superstars... Please come-a back to me..."*

There are moments a man can dodge and moments he cannot. I knelt beside my rival, close enough to touch, hands trembling at my sides like useless flags.

*"We are still superstars,"* I whispered. The lava nearly swallowed it. I said it again, because the first time was for him and the second time was for the record. *"...We're still superstars."*

A single tear slipped down Luigi's soot-streaked cheek. It caught the orange light, hung at his jaw, and dropped onto the hot stone with a tiny hiss. Gone.

Something in me did not hiss away. It stayed. It hurt. I reached out and gripped his shoulder, not shaking, not demanding, just holding on.

*"Hey. You're gonna be fine. We got you. You hear me? You're NOT gone."*
sections.waluigi_note: The quote stays exactly as filed because it is the session's spine. Luigi asked a question meant for Mario. I answered it anyway. That does not make me Mario, and thank every star in every registered sky for that. It means somebody in the room refused to let the question go unanswered while Luigi was bleeding hope onto a lava rock.

sections.name: VII. Home Means Carried
sections.overview:
*"Let's go home."*

The words did not solve anything. They did not find Mario, name the yellow cape, or explain why a garden would sit above fire. They did what useful words do when grand words fail: they gave feet a direction.

Wario lifted Luigi with a care that would have embarrassed him if anyone pointed at it. Mona took the other side until the burns made gripping impossible, then shifted to steady him by the back. Ashley flew ahead, checking the tunnels before we reached them. Kat and Ana kept to the high route when they could and dropped down when the rocks narrowed. Jimmy T brought up the rear, quieter now, hat pulled low.

I walked behind them all, watching every shadow. The fake Luigi had talked. That did not mean Bowser's compound had finished talking back. Every bend looked like another trap, every pipe like a mouth. Luigi winced with every few steps. Wario adjusted without being asked. Mona murmured encouragement. Ashley called back once that the path ahead was clear and then said it again louder because nobody believed in clear paths anymore.

The tunnel finally opened into cooler air. The night sky spread over us, star-pale through smoke. Luigi breathed like a man surfacing.

*"Fresh air... that's-a nice."*

We let him rest on a flat rock beyond the exit. The heat still glowed behind us. The question had changed: not *is Luigi alive* anymore, but *what happened to him, who wrote the note, and how fast can we get burns treated before Waluigi commits medical malpractice by glaring at them.*

*"Rest up,"* I told him. *"We need to figure what the hell happened to you. And who wrote that note."*
sections.waluigi_note: This is why the arc ends here. The rescue objective closes on the rock outside the tunnel. The mystery does not close; it turns into the next file. A clean ending is not the same thing as a solved problem. It is the place where the party stops dying long enough to choose the next problem on purpose.

sections.name: VIII. Dr. Toad, Apparently
sections.overview:
Jimmy T asked the practical question first, which is why he is valuable even when hopping badly over lava rocks.

*"What about getting him to a hospital?"*

Mona snapped into motion. Star Hill had a clinic close enough to reach before the burns stiffened further. Ashley flew ahead to guide the route. Wario put Luigi on his back, and Luigi held on with the miserable discipline of a man trying not to scream into someone else's neck.

We reached the clinic without an ambush, which felt suspicious but was medically convenient. A front-desk Toad saw Wario carrying a limp Luigi and began to inhale for a scream. I stepped in front of him.

*"He's ALIVE, you idiot!"*

The doctor arrived smiling. *"Dr. Toad, at your service!"*

I squinted. *"Doctor Toad. Is that really your name?"*

It certainly was, according to the only witness professionally motivated to insist. He moved fast after that: scissors through filthy bandages, clean water, salve, fresh wrapping. Luigi's face tightened every time the cloth lifted from a burn. Wario looked at the wall like he could intimidate pain by refusing to watch it. Mona explained too quickly. Ashley used the window instead of the door.

The verdict was better than it could have been and worse than anyone wanted. Serious but treatable. Mostly second-degree burns on arms and legs. Exhaustion, pain, and trauma delirium explaining the confusion. Fluids. Clean dressings. Two weeks of rest. Absolutely no adventuring.

Luigi winced at that last part harder than at some of the bandages. The doctor wrote [[prop:prop_dr_toad_luigi_burn_chart|the chart]] anyway.
sections.waluigi_note: I am suspicious of anyone whose profession and species produce the same business card. I am not suspicious of the treatment. Dr. Toad knew burns, knew delirium, and knew when the word Mario was a loaded hammer best left on the table for someone else to pick up.

sections.name: IX. Better Than This
sections.overview:
Then Dr. Toad asked why Luigi had been at the castle alone. Did he not usually travel with his brother?

The room went quiet so abruptly even the bottles on the shelf seemed to stop clinking. Luigi looked at me without turning his head, then at the sheets.

*"We... had an argument. I left on my own."*

The doctor apologized himself out of the room. Wise man, suspicious name. Ashley drifted toward the door to give space. Mona stayed close enough to help and far enough not to corner anyone. Wario leaned against the wall with his arms crossed, which is Wario for I am emotionally present and hate it.

I stood at the window for too long deciding whether to say Mario's name. Not yet. Luigi was burned, bandaged, and still half speaking to a person who was not there. A file can wait. A wound cannot.

*"Luigi,"* I said finally. *"I'm not... great at this."*

He laughed. A real laugh, short and broken at the end by pain.

*"Of course not. You're my rival, after all."*

I almost smiled. Wario saw it, because Wario sees weakness the way rats see kitchens. He pushed off the wall and came to the foot of the bed.

*"For what it's worth,"* he grunted, *"Mario's gone. We all know it. That doesn't mean you gotta be stupid about it."*

He looked from Luigi to me.

*"You two are both idiots, but... you're better than this."*

Mona's eyes shone. Luigi stared at the ceiling and did not argue. I swallowed what I wanted to say and filed what was true: the night had ended. The rescue was done. The next door was not Bowser's gate. It was a garden above fire, and a brother missing from a room where his name still hurt.
sections.waluigi_note: Wario's bedside speeches are short because if they get longer than four sentences they become invoices. This one did the job. Luigi heard it. I heard it. Neither of us thanked him, which is how Wario knows it mattered.
