name: The Tape and the Wario Files
title: The Tape and the Wario Files: Two Days in a Dark Room, a Notebook Read Aloud, and the Perspective of Greed
date: 20 Harvestide, 1035 BF - two days after the Star Hill clinic delivery
era: The Search for Mario / Post-Compound Fallout / The Garden Above the Fire
location: Waluigi's room and the adjoining kitchen, WarioWare company housing
summary:
Two days after Luigi was carried into Dr. Toad's Star Hill clinic, Waluigi did not leave his room. He sat in front of a VHS tape of the brothers' hallway argument and played it on loop - six times by the count in this filing, more by his own - with the curtains drawn and the sound low. Wario came in without knocking, ostensibly about a company meeting in the morning, and stayed for two days instead.

What that visit produced, in order: a notebook read aloud that turned out to contain poetry rather than scribbles; a glass of water and some garlic clippings offered as research; a search of the room that turned up never-sent letters and newspaper clippings with one name circled; and a single gold coin taped under a sticky note, drawn on the Star Festival fund, left on Waluigi's bed the year he won nothing.

The coin pulled the Mario Kart Massacre back up, and with it Wario's account of the phone calls he made to get out of it - the recordings the media later called the Wario Files. Then Wario, who had been told he learned nothing from the tapes, said what he had actually learned, and reframed the courier's note. 'The garden above the fire.' 'The star is not lost.' Read from the perspective of greed rather than heroism, the note stops describing a rescue and starts describing a hiding place. The star is not lost because it was taken. It is lost because somebody kept it.
description:
A downtime filing with no combat in it, filed at full length because the arc turns here. The previous session ended with Luigi alive, Mario absent, and a note nobody could read: 'The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire.' This session does not find Mario. It changes what the sentence means, which is worth more.

It also puts a primary source in the archive for the first time. The brothers' hallway argument has existed in these files only as the recalled testimony of a blue-painted impostor who was not in the room and had every reason to shade it. There is now a tape. The line-by-line reading of that tape is filed separately as an article analysis, because it deserves the room.

sections.name: I. Six Rewinds
sections.subtitle: a man, a chair, and the same ninety seconds
sections.overview:
The room had been dark for two days. Curtains drawn tight enough that nobody outside could tell whether the light was on. Coffee cups stacked on the nightstand in a column that had stopped being about coffee. The television on, the sound low, the tape running.

[Waluigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/waluigi) sat in the chair with his knees pulled up and his arms around them, cap tilted sideways, eyes dry and open. The tape had played three times. Maybe four. He had lost count, which is the detail that matters: this is an archivist, and archivists count things. He had stopped counting.

The screen cut to black. He stared at the dead screen for a full minute. Then he reached over and hit rewind, and [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi)'s voice filled the room again like a ghost with a grudge.

*"You thought that Koopa worked alone..."*

That is the opening line of the tape, and it is also the line Luigi threw at Waluigi on the lava bridge. The archive has had that sentence in it for two filings. This is the first time anyone has heard who said it first.

The tape itself is ninety seconds of corridor. A camera mounted high in the corner, the kind installed to watch a door rather than a conversation, so the two men in the frame are small and the ceiling is enormous. There is no establishing shot and no ending. It begins with both brothers already mid-sentence and it stops while one of them is still talking. Somebody chose both of those edges, and nothing in the footage explains who.

By the fourth pass Waluigi had stopped watching the brothers at all. He was watching the parts of the frame nobody was supposed to look at - the reflection in the glass at the end of the hall, the timecode ticking in the corner, the half-second where the image tears and reassembles. That is not grief. That is an archivist's reflex surviving inside a man who has otherwise stopped functioning, and it is the reason this filing exists at all.

He rewound it a fifth time. The cups did not move. Outside, somewhere below the window, the company yard ran a shift change and nobody in the room noticed.
sections.waluigi_note:
*I am not going to pretend to be objective about this section.* I was in the chair. I know what the room smelled like. Stale coffee and regret, and I am filing that phrase because it is accurate and because if I do not write it down somebody else will write something kinder and the record will be wrong.

Six rewinds. Wario says six. I would have said four. **He was counting and I was not, and that is the entire difference between us this week.**

sections.name: II. The Door Opens Without Knocking
sections.subtitle: "you alright, its pretty late"
sections.overview:
[Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) does not knock. He came in and said there was a company meeting in the morning, which is the kind of thing a person says when they have come for another reason and want a door out of the conversation.

*"Go away."*

*"I said I'm fine."*

He did not go away. He picked up the notebook off the desk, read the title, and started flipping. Waluigi came out of the chair fast enough to nearly tip it - and then stopped mid-lunge, hand out, because Wario had paused. Flipped back two pages. Forward again. The expression on him had gone from amusement to something quieter.

*"...The hell is this?"*

He read a line of it out loud. *"The stars don't shine without the dark. And I don't shine without-"* and then he stopped and asked *without what*, and got told to give it back, and did not.

Then he tossed it onto a pile of similar books in the corner and asked if it was a diary, which is the single most Wario way to handle another man's poetry.

The door had not been locked. That is worth recording, because Waluigi locks doors, and for two days he had not. [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) came in the way he comes into every room he intends to own - shoulder first, talking before the hinge had finished swinging, a clipboard in one hand that he never once looked at. The company meeting was at nine. The company meeting was the excuse and both of them knew it inside four seconds.

What he did next is the part that matters. He did not open the curtains. He did not turn on the overhead light, or turn off the tape, or say any of the six sentences a person is supposed to say to somebody sitting in the dark. He crossed the room, looked at the screen for a while without comment, and then picked up the nearest object on the desk, which happened to be a notebook, and started reading it out loud in the flat voice of a man reading a delivery manifest.

It was not a manifest. Three lines in, the flatness came off his voice on its own, and he slowed down, and he did not seem to notice that he had.
sections.waluigi_note:
It is NOT a diary. It is a **working notebook**. There is a difference and the difference is that a diary is for feelings and a notebook is for *evidence*, and the fact that some of the evidence rhymes is nobody's business.

He said he would not share it. I am choosing, for reasons I decline to examine, to believe him.

sections.name: III. Water and Garlic
sections.subtitle: the worst research in the archive, offered sincerely
sections.overview:
The intervention, such as it was, was not a speech. It was: *you gotta talk to someone eventually*, and *you've been locked in here for two days*, and - the part that actually landed - *even I think that's messed up, and I lock myself in rooms too*.

Then he yelled at an empty hallway to clear the room, discovered [Mona](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mona) had already left, and scratched the back of his head.

*"Luigi's gonna be okay."* Not a joke. Not a provocation. Stated like a fact, by a man who does not state comforting things.

In the kitchen he put the kettle on and produced garlic clippings, explaining that he had been doing his own research and that garlic is supposed to be good for stress. Also that it keeps vampires away, and that if he was going to help with this he might as well keep the creepy stuff at bay.

Waluigi drank the water. The notebook went on the counter between them like a truce flag, with one condition attached: *don't read any more of it.*

The kitchen is four steps from the bed and it is where this session actually turns. Wario filled a glass from the tap, put it down hard enough to be deniable as kindness, and then went through the cupboard and came back with garlic clippings - the dried outer skins nobody keeps - and set those down too, and announced that they were for research. Neither man defined the research. Neither man had to.

This is the whole grammar of the visit. Wario does not have the vocabulary for the thing he came to do, so he substitutes objects for it: a glass, a handful of skins, later a coin. Each one is delivered with an insult attached as packaging, and the insult is the receipt that lets both of them pretend the delivery was a transaction.

Waluigi drank the whole glass without stopping, which told the room how long it had been since he had drunk anything. Then he said thank you, and Wario said *"don't,"* and that was the closest either of them got to naming it.
sections.waluigi_note:
For the record the garlic research is **worthless**. Garlic does nothing for stress. It does nothing for vampires either, and I say that as somebody who has been inside [Raventree Manor](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/raventree_manor) and watched what actually works.

He looked it up though. That is the part I cannot get around. **He went and looked something up, badly, on purpose, for me.**

sections.name: IV. The Room, Searched
sections.subtitle: clippings, letters, and one name circled
sections.overview:
Wario came back into the room later and went over it properly, the way he goes over a vault.

What was on the walls: newspaper clippings, old tournament results from the Mushroom Kingdom, each one circled where Waluigi's name appeared. What was on the desk: a half-eaten plate of spaghetti and a stack of handwritten letters, crumpled, none of them sent.

He unfolded one. *"I know you probably don't care about any of this but I had to say something before I lost my mind."*

He put it back exactly where he found it. That is filed deliberately - *exactly where he found it* - because it is out of character and because it is the second time in two days he handled something of Waluigi's more carefully than he handles gold.

Then he backed toward the door, got caught, turned around, and said *"Your handwriting's terrible,"* and dropped the letter like it had burned him.

The search was not subtle and was not meant to be. Wario went through the room the way he goes through a vault: drawers out and stacked on the floor, the wardrobe emptied onto the bed, the loose board by the radiator found in under a minute by a man who has spent a career finding loose boards. Waluigi did not stop him. He stayed in the chair with the tape running and let it happen, which is its own kind of statement.

The inventory, as filed: eleven letters, none of them sent, none of them addressed to anyone in the room. A stack of newspaper clippings going back years, folded to the same column each time, with one name circled in pencil hard enough to emboss the page behind it. A tournament bracket with every round filled in except the last. And, at the bottom of the box, under all of it, a thing Wario looked at for a long moment and then put back exactly as he had found it, face down, and did not mention again.

He has still not mentioned it. This filing notes the omission and does not fill it.
sections.waluigi_note:
My handwriting is **fine**.

The letters are not addressed to anybody. That is not a coincidence and I am not going to explain it in a public filing.

sections.name: V. The Coin
sections.subtitle: Star Festival fund, no note, left on a bed
sections.overview:
Taped under the corner of a sticky note on the notepad: a single gold coin. Wario found it because Wario finds coins.

Waluigi took it off him and flipped it over and went pale, because the coin is drawn on the **Star Festival fund** - and that is a real fund with real accounting attached to it, not a keepsake.

The story came out slowly, sitting on the edge of the bed, the coin rolling between his fingers:

> It was after the tournament. Everyone won something. Mario had his trophy. Luigi had his trophy. Waluigi did not win anything that year. And afterward somebody left this on his bed. No note. Just the coin.

Wario, trying to be helpful, called it a participation trophy. That went about as well as it deserved to.

*"Someone went out of their way to-"* and then he stopped himself, and swallowed, and said it did not matter.

He also said, earlier and more quietly, the thing this section is actually filed for: **"It was the last time things made sense."**

The coin was taped to the underside of a sticky note, and the sticky note was blank. One gold piece, Star Festival mint, drawn on the festival fund in a year when Waluigi placed in nothing and won nothing and was, by the official record, not a participant. Somebody had signed it out of a fund they were entitled to spend, walked it up a flight of stairs, and left it on a bed in an empty room.

Waluigi has kept it for years without spending it and without explaining it. He did not explain it now either. He turned it over twice, put it on the nightstand between them, and said nothing, and let Wario read the mint mark himself.

Wario read it. The archive would like to record what his face did at that moment, and cannot, because the only witness was sitting behind him and has declined to characterise it. What is on the record is that he did not make a joke, and that the gap before he spoke again was long enough that the tape in the other room reached the end of its loop and cut to black unattended.
sections.waluigi_note:
The coin is evidence. I want that established in the record because the moment it becomes sentiment it stops being useful.

**Somebody with access to the Star Festival fund knew I had won nothing and knew which bed was mine.** That is a very short list of people. I have had this coin for years and I have never once written that sentence down. It is written down now.

sections.name: VI. The Wario Files
sections.subtitle: the Mario Kart Massacre, the faked death, and the phone calls
sections.overview:
The coin pulled the Mario Kart Massacre up with it, and Wario's own history with it: he had to fake his own death to get clear, and he had to pull strings to manage that.

The recordings the media later called the Wario Files are a matter of public record and this filing will not reproduce them in full. The load-bearing facts for this archive's purposes:

- A televised Mario Kart broadcast became a mass-casualty event on the eleventh of September, two years before the trial.
- President Wario, drunk and driving, called his daughter first - before authorities, before medics - to arrange the aftermath.
- The plan was a faked death: the comatose angle, then waking while the medics were distracted, then out through the ambulance.
- His daughter, who controlled the network the massacre was airing on, spent the rest of that day making calls: a lawyer to stall the press, a contract killer for four named targets, and a supplier.
- The cover story - President Wario dead by his own hand, in terror of facing justice - was accepted by the kingdom without a serious question.
- At trial she interrupted the court to insist, on the record, that her father was not dead. Then the judge was shot.

*"Seems like her coverup worked,"* Wario said, and laughed.

*"Yeah, real comedy genius over there."*

The Wario Files, as the media eventually named them, are not one recording but a run of phone calls placed over a single afternoon by a man trying very hard not to be on a starting grid. He made them from a company line, which is why they exist: the line logged everything, and nobody thought to stop it. He called in a debt, then a favour, then a threat, in that order, escalating politely until something moved.

His account of them here is unusually complete and unusually unashamed. He did not present the calls as a scandal he survived. He presented them as a procedure that worked, which is a considerably stranger thing to sit across a kitchen from. He listed who he called. He listed what each one cost him. He remembered the costs to the coin, years later, without checking a ledger.

Waluigi wrote the list down. That is the first time in this session that he picked up a pencil, and he has not put it down since.
sections.waluigi_note:
Two things and then I will leave this alone.

**One.** The whole kingdom just *accepted* it. A president dies conveniently, on the day of a televised massacre, and nobody pulls the thread. I have spent my career being told I am paranoid by people who swallowed that whole.

**Two.** He laughed. I want to be angry about that and I cannot entirely manage it, because I have listened to the tape in my own room six times and laughing is one of the two available options.

sections.name: VII. The Perspective of Greed
sections.subtitle: what Wario actually learned, and what it does to the note
sections.overview:
Waluigi told Wario he had learned nothing from the tapes. Wario smiled and said that Luigi was still in hospital, that Waluigi had locked himself in a room, and that *he* had learned something.

Then he explained it, and the room changed.

The courier's note has been read in this archive as a rescue instruction since the day it was recovered: *The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire.* A heroic sentence. Mario, hiding to protect something, leaving a trail for someone to follow.

Wario's reading: **run it as greed instead.**

Under that reading the sentence inverts. *The star is not lost* stops being reassurance and becomes an inventory note. The star is not lost because it was stolen or destroyed or hidden by an enemy. It is not lost because somebody still **has** it. And if Mario went east after the fountain, and has stayed gone this long, then *the garden above the fire* is not a description of where he was taken.

It is a description of where he is keeping it.

*"Greed. Of course that's your angle."* But Waluigi did not look away, and he had the pencil out, and he was running the numbers.

*"And make it good - I'm not chasing another wild Wario theory across a lava field."*

The reframing is worth setting out slowly, because the whole arc now rests on it. The courier's note reads: *"The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire."* Every reading the archive has filed so far treated that as a rescue instruction written by an ally - a location, a reassurance, a map fragment addressed to people who intend to go and get something back.

Wario read it as an inventory line. He has written notes like this. He has written them about property. *The star is not lost* is not comfort, in his reading; it is a status. It is the sentence you write when an asset is still on the books and still where you left it, and the reason you write it down at all is that somebody paid to have it moved and wants confirmation the move held.

Under that reading the second sentence stops being a riddle and starts being an address, and the first sentence stops being hope and starts being a receipt. The star is not lost because it was taken. It is lost because somebody still has it, and is keeping it somewhere warm and high and difficult to reach, and has written to confirm it is still there.

Waluigi ran the numbers for six minutes and did not find the hole. He has filed the reading as the working theory of the arc, under protest, in his own handwriting, which he maintains is fine.
sections.waluigi_note:
I believe him.

I have written that sentence three times tonight and deleted it twice. **For once in my miserable life I believe someone who isn't me,** and that should frighten me considerably more than it does.

Here is the part I keep circling. If the note is a hiding place and not a rescue, then everything downstream of it is wrong - the search pattern, the assumption that Mario is a victim in this, the reason we have been reading the fountain as an ambush site instead of a *departure* point. How many people have died because nobody asked the right question until a disgraced dead man in a basement pointed his finger and laughed?

I hate that it makes sense.

This is the whole recording. The archive has argued about this conversation for two filings on the strength of one witness who was not present, and the correction to that is not a better summary - it is the thing itself, in order, so that anybody who wants to check a reading against the source can do it without asking permission.

The transcription convention: speech exactly as spoken, including the stumbles. Mario's accent is written the way it sounds because smoothing it out is already an edit. Stage business in italics is what is visible on the tape, not what anybody reported afterwards. Where the two of them talk over each other, the tape is marked and the lines are given in the order they begin.

Two features of the recording are preserved here rather than repaired, because they are evidence. The silhouette passage is marked where it begins and ends. The recording's final frame is marked where it stops. Neither is a transcription failure.

aftermath:
Waluigi left the room. The company meeting in the morning went ahead and is not recorded here because nothing happened at it worth filing.

The tape stays in Waluigi's possession and is now logged as an exhibit rather than a personal effect, which means it can be cited and has to be produced on request. The notebook is not logged, by agreement.

The search for Mario continues on a changed premise. Every previous sweep assumed a man who had been taken or who was hiding to protect somebody. The greed reading assumes a man who left with something and does not intend to give it back. Those two searches do not look in the same places.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. I lost two days and I am not going to pretend otherwise.** The tape does not change when you watch it again. I knew that by the third rewind and I did it three more times, and the only honest reason is that while the tape is running the argument is not over yet.

**2. Wario did the single most competent thing anybody has done in this arc, and he did it with garlic.** He did not talk me out of the room. He brought water, stood in the doorway being annoying, refused to leave, and waited. I have been on the other side of a dozen interventions run by professionals and not one of them worked. This one worked because it did not announce itself.

**3. The coin is the oldest open case in my own files and I have never once worked it.** Someone with access to the Star Festival fund knew I had won nothing and knew which bed was mine. I have had years to pull that thread. I have never pulled it, because I preferred the version where it meant something to the version where it turns out to be an accounting error. That is not archival practice. That is cowardice with a filing system.

**4. The greed reading is correct and I resent it.** For two filings this note has been a rescue instruction, because we read it as people who wanted Mario to be worth rescuing. Wario read it as a man who wanted to know where the valuable thing was, and got a cleaner answer in one evening than the rest of us managed in a month. *The star is not lost* is not comfort. It is an inventory line.

**5. Luigi is still burning in a hospital bed.** I have spent this filing on a coin, a notebook and a tape, and the whole time there has been a man in Star Hill with burns down one side who asked, at the end of the last session, whether we are still superstars. I do not have an answer. I am filing the question again so that it stays open and so that nobody gets to quietly stop asking it.

description:
*The archive is backfilling the room before the assault because the dragon is not the opening move. The opening move was a family resemblance used as a key. Bowser woke on his throne believing he had finally escaped one session of nonsense. The castle had used that session to change sides. WAH.*

The false Bowser Jr. session had ended, or appeared to end, with Bowser exhausted enough to sleep where he sat. When he woke, the throne's stone arms were warm beneath his claws and the banners over the hall were hanging in the wrong order. He had the dry taste of spent fire in his mouth. Somewhere below, a bell rang once and stopped.

Bowser blinked at the empty space in front of him. Then he looked toward the door.

The door opened before he called for it.

That was the first thing that made him stand.

sections.name: I. The Throne Room Was the Target
sections.overview:
This was not an anonymous castle corridor and not a prank that stayed at the edge of the fortress. The target was Bowser’s throne room. The fake Bowser Jr. session was used as an infiltration key: the Jester’s performance gave the conspirators a reason to enter, move around, and keep Bowser’s attention on the supposed heir while Mimbus and Fawthful gained position at the throne. By the time Bowser understood that Bowser Jr. was not there, the room had already been breached politically and physically.

Saying that the castle was simply lost is an understatement. The attackers had penetrated the room that represented Bowser’s command, used the false heir to get past the normal suspicion of the court, and made the throne room answer to another operation before the dragon ever arrived. Bowser still held the room long enough to fight and issue orders, but he was defending a throne that had been infiltrated from inside.
sections.waluigi_note: When an army breaches a palace, they usually want the treasury or the king. Fawful's mutineers wanted the empty throne and the broadcast horn.

sections.name: II. The False Heir
sections.overview:
The Jester came in wearing the aftermath of the Bowser Jr. performance like a costume that had not yet been put away. Mimbus followed. Fawthful was already waiting beyond the threshold, where the corridor lamps had been dimmed to the colour of old bruises.

Bowser's first question was not complicated. It was the one question the performance had been designed to prevent him from asking earlier: where was his son?

The answer was not a person. It was a laugh, a gesture toward the empty corridor, and the sudden recognition that every detail Bowser had accepted during the session had been arranged to keep him looking at the wrong face. The Jester had supplied the shape of the heir. Mimbus had supplied the movement around him. Fawthful had supplied the reason.

The room went quiet in the way a room goes quiet when everyone inside it has already decided what will happen next.

Bowser's shell scraped the throne's stone back as he rose. He did not roar. That made the Jester stop laughing.

**“You used my son’s face to get inside my house.”**

Fawthful answered from the hall. The answer was not an apology. It was a declaration that the house was already theirs in every way that mattered.
sections.waluigi_note: Parading an impersonator through the hallways works until the real father wakes up from his nap.

sections.name: III. A Castle That Answered Elsewhere
sections.overview:
Bowser reached for the command bell and heard a response from below before he touched it. Boots moved in the west passage. A portcullis dropped somewhere under the kitchens. The left-hand torches went out together. There were too many changes for a single prank and too much timing for a panic.

The castle had not merely admitted strangers. It had been taught to answer to them.

Bowser found a torn garrison sheet beneath the throne steps, its seal broken and its route marks overwritten. The paper is filed as [[prop:prop_castle_betrayal_roster|the garrison sheet with the altered routes]]. It named doors that should have been locked, defenders who had been moved without his order, and a passage from the lower barracks to the inner wall that only a traitor could have opened from inside.

Mimbus stood close enough to see the paper. The Jester stood far enough away to run.

Fawthful did not run. Fawthful looked at the throne, then at Bowser, with the patience of somebody waiting for a crown to admit it had become furniture.

The compromised castle was the point of the whole deception. The false heir had not been a private insult. It had been a screen drawn across the king's attention while the garrison, the routes, and the doors changed hands. Bowser had spent the session defending an image of his family while somebody else had been measuring his walls.
sections.waluigi_note: Half the garrison was taking orders from a bean merchant in a cape while the other half was wondering why the lunch gong hadn't sounded.

sections.name: IV. Cackletta Opens the Room
sections.overview:
The first spell struck the floor between Bowser and the corridor. It came in green, folded light, and it split the black stone without producing a flame. The second spell struck the throne.

Bowser moved before the third.

He hit the arm of the throne hard enough to break the carved claw from it, came over the dais, and filled the room with fire. The Jester vanished behind a curtain. Mimbus threw up a shield. Fawthful stepped sideways rather than back. From the far arch, Cackletta entered the light with magic already gathered around both hands.

That entrance changed the shape of the room. This was not a coup being announced to a tired king. It was a battle being started in a place where the enemy had already counted the doors.

Bowser's fire met Cackletta's first spell and turned the air white. Stone dust came down from the ceiling. The banners caught at their lower edges. Mimbus shouted for the inner guard, and three voices answered from the wrong side of the wall.

Bowser put one claw into the cracked throne and pulled himself upright through the smoke.

**“Nobody takes my castle while I’m standing in it.”**

The next strike came from Cackletta. The throne room disappeared behind light, smoke, and the sound of a king charging toward the breach.
sections.waluigi_note: Cackletta's entrance was not subtle. Lightning through the rose window and a cackle that cracked the ceiling plaster.

sections.name: V. The Castle Had Already Changed Sides
sections.overview:
Bowser’s first mistake was not believing the Jester. It was believing that the performance had an ending. A false Bowser Jr. could be ridiculous, insulting, or both; those were ordinary court problems. The unusual thing was the silence after the act. There was no clean dismissal, no familiar argument, no troop captain arriving to complain that the throne room had been used as a stage again. The pause was not empty. It was the room making time for people who had already moved into position.

The altered route sheet makes the timing visible after the fact. A west passage had been opened from inside. Two defenders had been removed from their posts without replacement names. The throne approach had been permitted under the cover of an heir session, but the royal seal that should have made that permission legitimate was absent. None of those marks, by itself, names a traitor. Together they show that the castle was being taught to obey a different instruction while its king was looking at a face he thought he recognised.

That is why the Jester’s part cannot be filed as a prank. The performance did not need to convince every witness that the false heir was real. It only needed to keep Bowser from asking the next question while the castle’s doors and corridors answered somebody else. Mimbus belongs to the same mechanism. The record places Mimbus between the theatrical deception and the physical compromise: close enough to the lie to benefit from it, and close enough to the routes to know what the lie had bought.
sections.waluigi_note: The Koopa Troop didn't lose the fortification to siege engines; they lost it to red armbands distributed during the night shift.

sections.name: VI. The Three People at the Door
sections.overview:
When Bowser woke, the people waiting outside the throne room did not form a normal delegation. The Jester carried the residue of the false Bowser Jr. performance. Mimbus carried the quieter part of the operation, the part that did not need a costume. Fawthful stood beyond them as though the castle had already accepted Fawthful’s right to be there. That arrangement mattered more than any speech. It made the deception, the access, and the proposed succession one continuous act.

Bowser’s response was not a legal challenge. He checked the room, the hall, and the distance to the nearest bell. He recognised that the castle was still physically his and institutionally uncertain. The distinction is the hinge of the backfill. A king can own a throne and still lose the next corridor if the garrison has been moved under an instruction he did not issue.

Fawthful’s claim therefore arrived before the battle as a claim about permission. The castle was being treated as available. The false heir supplied the excuse for opening the way; the compromised routes supplied the practical access; the takeover language supplied the reason. The record does not identify every conspirator, and it should not. It establishes something narrower and more useful: the assault had an inside before it had a breach.
sections.waluigi_note: Three sentries watching the throne room double doors, knowing that whoever walked out was going to demand their oaths.

sections.name: VII. Cackletta Makes the Lie Public
sections.overview:
The revelation might still have remained a confrontation inside a damaged court if Cackletta had not opened the fight. Her arrival changed the archive’s category for the scene. Before the first spell, Bowser could still have treated the false heir, the altered routes, and Fawthful’s presence as a coup attempt that might be forced back into the language of succession. After the spell, the throne room was an active battlefield.

Cackletta did not answer every question. She did not identify each guard who had moved, explain the missing seal, or turn Mimbus’s role into a complete confession. What she did was make delay impossible. A spell crossing the throne room gave Bowser a threat he could answer with force, and it gave the people outside the room a reason to stop pretending that the castle had merely suffered an administrative irregularity.

Bowser held the room long enough for the next record to exist. That is not the same as winning the coup. The castle was compromised, the outer force was already moving, and the opening exchange had made clear that this was not a family dispute that could be settled by finding the real Bowser Jr. The first filing ends at the moment the joke becomes a military operation.
sections.waluigi_note: Making a mutiny official by announcing it over the castle acoustics. When the lie is louder than the truth, the soldiers start checking their pensions.

sections.name: VIII. Why This Backfill Belongs in the Archive
sections.overview:
The exact hour is not recorded. The placement is inferred from the existing 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF chain, and the assault follows this throne-room compromise in the recovered sequence. That uncertainty is part of the record, not a reason to put the event on the present 1040 BF page.

This backfill also explains why the later assault cannot be read as a dragon suddenly appearing outside an otherwise loyal fortress. The dragon was the loud part. The quieter opening was the false heir, the missing seal, and the route that answered before Bowser gave an order. The next filing begins with the wall coming down because the inside had already been made answerable to someone else.
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi filed this historical backfill because an empire doesn't collapse from the outside; it rots from the second floor down. WAH.

**The switch is a perfect castle joke because it is a real command failure.** A self-destruct control with three labels, two identical toggles, and no surviving certainty about which is which is not a plan. Bowser left it alone and got the only decision right that the room could offer.

**Fawthful did not mistake the breach for the end.** The ruler-then-god declaration tells the archive what the dragon and the traitors were for: not destruction, but succession. The castle was the first throne in a larger sentence.

sections.name: I. The Throne Room Was Breached
sections.overview:
The recovered assault took place in Bowser’s throne room. The first breach was the false Bowser Jr. session: the fake heir gave the infiltrators a plausible reason to enter and kept Bowser looking at a family performance while Fawthful, Mimbus, and the hostile operation gained access to the seat of power. That is why the throne-room compromise is Session I and this assault is Session II. The second breach was the dragon breaking through the throne-room window and wall.

This is more severe than saying that the castle was lost. A castle can be abandoned, retaken, or described as a military position. The throne room being breached means the king’s actual command space was penetrated, its doors and routes were turned against him, and the invaders could make their claim in front of the throne while Bowser was still fighting. Bowser did not surrender the castle. He ordered the garrison away from the dragon so there would be survivors to carry the kingdom forward, then came back to challenge the occupation.


The dragon came through the smoke with the sound of stone being dragged across stone. Its head cleared the outer wall first. Then one claw hooked over the battlement and the wall began to shed blocks into the courtyard.

Bowser saw his troops turn toward it. He also saw the shape of that turn: Goombas bunching under the gatehouse, Koopas lifting their shields, and three defenders looking over their shoulders for the corridor they planned to use when the king stopped watching.

**“Back!”** Bowser roared. **“Get away from the dragon!”**

The command moved faster than the fear. Koopa shells locked into a line and rolled sideways across the yard, making a low barrier between the dragon's reach and the barracks door. Goombas dropped flat, ran beneath the swinging edge of the dragon's jaw, and hauled wounded soldiers by their belts toward the stairs. It was not a beautiful formation. It worked because the small bodies went where the large body could not.

The retreat order is filed as [[prop:prop_bowser_retreat_order|Bowser’s order to pull the line away from the dragon]]. It is short, direct, and written for troops who have no time to admire the king's phrasing.
sections.waluigi_note: Masonry caving inward and magma dripping through the cracked ceiling. A classic royal reception in dark lands.

sections.name: II. Fire, Stone, and the First Retreat
sections.overview:
Bowser planted both feet in the courtyard and breathed.

Fire rolled out of him in a broad orange sheet. It struck the dragon's throat, lit the broken masonry, and turned the rain of dust into sparks. The dragon recoiled just far enough for the front line to move. Bowser followed with a ground pound that travelled through the courtyard like a dropped bell. The flagstones buckled. The dragon's hooked claw slipped. Two Goombas shouted in triumph and immediately remembered they were supposed to be retreating.

A Magikoopa snapped a wand toward the eastern stair. Purple light caught six Koopas and moved them three floors upward in a single blink. Another Magikoopa teleported the wounded behind the kitchens. A third tried to move a supply cart, lost the cart, and delivered only the wheels.

The useful magic was not elegant. It was distance. Every teleport made a few bodies harder for the dragon to reach and a little easier for the traitors to count.

The traitors showed themselves when the inner gate opened from the wrong side. A Koopa with a red armband waved the attackers through. A Goomba pulled the chain on the second portcullis and then stood aside as if the motion had been an accident. The castle's own corridors began sending people toward the breach.

Bowser saw the red armband. He saw the dragon behind it. He did not have time to ask how many more there were.
sections.waluigi_note: Lava pumps failing in sequence while the rearguard tried to remember which corridor led to the emergency stairs.

sections.name: III. The Hammer Bro Knows When to Leave
sections.overview:
The Hammer Bro held the west passage until the ceiling shook. He threw a hammer into the dragon's eye, missed, hit a traitor, and did not stop to find out whether the result was politically complicated. When the second wall cracked, he backed toward the evacuation stair.

Bowser shouted for him to hold.

The Hammer Bro shouted back that he had held.

Then he retreated.

The retreat was not cowardice. It was the first honest order anybody had followed all night. The west passage was no longer a position. It was a place where the ceiling was about to become a floor. The Hammer Bro took the surviving Goombas with him, and the Koopas closed their shells behind them long enough for the Magikoopas to teleport the last wounded defender out.

Fawthful's forces followed through the broken gate. Mimbus came with them. The Jester was nowhere in the smoke. Cackletta's magic flashed above the inner wall, turning the stone red from the inside.
sections.waluigi_note: A veteran non-commissioned officer knows the exact difference between battlefield courage and being turned into charcoal.

sections.name: IV. The Evacuation Plan and the Switch
sections.overview:
Bowser reached the lower command room with the dragon's roar shaking dust from the map cabinets. He wanted a counterattack. The remaining officers wanted a route. Both positions were honest. Only one of them kept the troops alive.

The evacuation plan spread across the table: barracks first, wounded by Magikoopa teleport, stores through the lava tunnel, rear guard at the inner stair, and nobody touching the switch until the last defender was clear.

The switch sat beneath a metal cover beside the map case. A painted label above it read **SELF-DESTRUCT**. A second, smaller label underneath read **DO NOT USE FOR LIGHTING**. A third label, written in a different hand, said **THIS ONE MAY BE THE LIGHTING**.

The label is filed as [[prop:prop_castle_self_destruct_switch_label|the switch plate that could not agree with itself]].

Bowser stared at it.

A Goomba said the switch destroyed the castle. A Koopa said the switch opened the emergency lamps. A Magikoopa said teleporting the switch would be safer. Somebody had already tried, and the switch had teleported back into its bracket.

Bowser lifted the cover and found two identical red toggles.

Nobody knew which one was the real switch.

That was the joke. It was also the evacuation plan's worst possible ending.

Bowser closed the cover without touching either toggle and ordered the troops out through the lava tunnel. The castle could be rebuilt. A castle full of defenders who had been blown up by their own labelled furniture would be harder to explain.
sections.waluigi_note: The castle emergency lever had been rewired to an external fuse box that nobody in the room recognized.

sections.name: V. The Breach and the Claim
sections.overview:
The throne-room wall gave way before the last line cleared the lower hall. The sound was not an explosion. It was a long stone groan followed by the collapse of everything that had been pretending to be one wall.

Fawthful walked through the opening in the throne-room wall with dust on the shoulders and the dragon behind him. Mimbus came at his side. Cackletta's spellwork crawled along the broken masonry in green lines. The traitors had stopped hiding. The remaining loyalists had stopped pretending there was a clean way to win.

Bowser came back up the stair instead of leaving with the first group.

Fawthful looked over the breached castle, the retreating troops, the open corridors and the throne room being torn open around them. Then Fawthful described the future as if it had already been signed: Bowser's kingdom would become the first piece, the world would become the estate, and the name on the throne would eventually be the name people prayed to.

**“Ruler first,”** Fawthful said. **“God after.”**

Mimbus stood beside the claim. The dragon lowered its head behind them. Bowser answered with fire, not because the fire could close the breach, but because the alternative was letting the invader mistake evacuation for surrender.

The flames filled the broken gate. Fawthful did not step back.

The throne room was breached. The castle’s troops were moving. The switch remained untouched. The battle was not over.
sections.waluigi_note: Stamping an eviction notice on smoking stone while the artillery was still hitting the exterior battlements.

sections.name: VI. The Dragon Changed the Geometry
sections.overview:
The dragon was not merely a stronger soldier at the gate. It changed which spaces counted as safe. A wall that had protected the courtyard became a source of falling stone. A straight line toward the barracks became a path through a creature’s reach. The defenders could not meet the dragon on the terms the dragon offered, and Bowser’s first useful command was therefore a refusal to let the garrison perform bravery in the most convenient place for the attacker.

The retreat order is short because the order is a map. Goombas moved wounded troops under the gatehouse and through the spaces the dragon’s head could not occupy. Koopas locked shells into a barrier, not to defeat the dragon, but to make one more body-length of time. Magikoopas spent teleportation on living defenders and equipment that mattered to the evacuation. None of these actions looks like a heroic charge when separated from the whole. Together they kept the assault from becoming an immediate collapse.

Bowser’s fire breath did not end the dragon. It did something more practical: it forced the attacker to react while the smaller bodies moved. The ground pound did the same on the ground. Stone broke, dust rose, and the courtyard became harder for a large enemy to read. The king was not trying to make the battlefield beautiful. He was buying a route through it.
sections.waluigi_note: When a winged reptile the size of a cathedral lands on the parapet, standard defensive tactics become purely theoretical.

sections.name: VII. The Order That Saved the Line
sections.overview:
The most important sentence in the retreat order is the first one: pull back from the dragon. It rejects the instinct to hold the wall because the wall is there. A compromised castle creates a dangerous loyalty test. Soldiers want to prove that they will not abandon their post, commanders want to prove that the fortress is still theirs, and an attacker wants both impulses to remain fixed long enough for the dragon to do the work.

Bowser’s order breaks that test. The line is allowed to move. Koopas protect the withdrawal, Goombas carry the wounded, and the Magikoopas move people rather than wasting their limited teleportation on objects that can be replaced. A Hammer Bro retreats when the wall becomes a ceiling. The filing records that departure without turning it into betrayal: knowing where the floor is can be a form of discipline when the alternative is being buried under the command to stand still.

The loyalists do not leave because they have stopped caring about the castle. They leave because the evacuation route is the part of the castle that can still be made to answer. The order converts a lost outer wall into a chance to keep the interior from becoming a mass grave.
sections.waluigi_note: An orderly retreat through three layers of blast doors is the only thing standing between an army and an autopsy.

sections.name: VIII. Traitors, Corridors, and the Breach
sections.overview:
The assault has two forces moving at once. The dragon and the visible troops break the outside. Traitors and compromised routes make the inside unreliable. Goombas and Koopas therefore fight two battles: one against the attackers in front of them and another against the uncertainty behind the next door. A corridor can be a shelter, a trap, or an evacuation lane depending on who reached it first.

That is why the Magikoopa teleportation matters beyond spectacle. Every moved defender is a person removed from a corridor that may already belong to the traitors. Every wounded soldier carried under the gatehouse is a witness who can later say which route opened and which order was obeyed. The evacuation does not restore the chain of command, but it keeps enough of the chain alive to make the investigation possible.

When the wall gives way, the breach is real and the castle is not surrendered. Fawthful’s forces reach the inner routes, but the operation has not yet become a settled government. Bowser’s troops have been pulled toward survival, the Hammer Bro has withdrawn with the surviving line, and the self-destruct control remains untouched because nobody can prove which red toggle does what.
sections.waluigi_note: Sentry posts manned by troops wearing fresh red armbands who suddenly forgot the challenge response.

sections.name: IX. The Switch Nobody Trusted
sections.overview:
The self-destruct-switch gag is funny only because the timing is terrible. The plate says SELF-DESTRUCT. It also says not to use the switch for lighting. Then it adds that one of the two identical red toggles may in fact be the lighting. A castle under assault does not need a philosophical problem above its evacuation controls. It needs a confirmed control and a person authorised to use it.

Bowser leaves both toggles alone. That choice is not cowardice and not indecision in the simple sense. A wrong press could kill the troops he is trying to move, destroy evidence of the internal compromise, or hand the attackers a ruin they could claim as a victory. The switch remains a live question because the label cannot tell the truth consistently enough to justify a hand on it.

The plate is consequently filed as an exhibit rather than a punchline. It shows the state of command at the exact moment the castle needs command most: a royal fortress with a dragon at the wall, a split garrison, and an emergency control whose warning label has become another source of uncertainty.
sections.waluigi_note: An iron toggle covered in grease and dried blood that promised to flood the trench but might just detonate the boiler.

sections.name: X. Fawthful and Mimbus at the Broken Wall
sections.overview:
The confrontation after the breach is not a clean victory speech. Fawthful and Mimbus appear where the castle’s physical damage and political damage meet. Bowser has not been removed from the throne by a formal vote, but the attackers are speaking as though occupation and legitimacy can be made identical by standing in the right room.

Fawthful’s ruler-then-god plan gives the assault its scale. The castle is not the final prize. It is the first seat, the proof that a throne can be taken, held, and converted into an argument for worship. Mimbus’s presence keeps the earlier deception attached to the later claim. The false heir was not an isolated performance, and the dragon was not an isolated siege weapon. They were parts of one attempt to make the castle consent after its king had stopped consenting.

Bowser answers from the breach rather than from a secure throne room. That is the important image in the historical record. He is still the ruler of the castle in the sense that matters to the defenders, but he is defending a place that no longer behaves as a single body. The battle ends its recovered section with the plan exposed, not completed.
sections.waluigi_note: Standing on the rubble in matching cloaks, watching the firestorm like two landlords admiring a fresh renovation.

sections.name: XI. Limits of the Recovered Record
sections.overview:
The archive does not have a complete traitor list, a confirmed identity for every attacker, or an exact hour for either filing. It does have the retreat order, the altered route sheet, the switch label, the sequence from false heir to breach, and the ruler-then-god statement. Those pieces support a careful conclusion: the castle was compromised from inside, the evacuation was deliberate, and Fawthful’s campaign was aimed at succession before divinity.

The current 1040 BF record places Bowser elsewhere, operating in the Shadow Estate. This article is therefore a historical reconstruction of the 1035 BF assault, not a report that the dragon is currently at Bowser’s wall.
sections.waluigi_note: Half the parchment rolls were scorched by flame and the ink on the roster was smudged by hydraulic fluid.

sections.name: XII. Recovered Scene: The Castle After the False Heir
sections.overview:
The assault record begins after the false Bowser Jr. session, not before it. The fake heir had been used to infiltrate Bowser’s throne room; this was the same room where Fawthful was already standing when the defenders understood that the castle had become a battlefield. The room was not merely occupied in the abstract. The throne, the window, the command routes, and the king’s own soldiers were all inside the fight. A Hammer Bro kept throwing hammers because that was the order he had been given. Another voice warned that there were too many attackers to count.

“Are you sure?” Bowser asked, looking past the hammer flight toward Mimbus.

The answer came from the window.

The dragon broke through the throne-room window, scattering glass and black stone across the hall. Bowser answered with a ground pound that shook the floor under everyone’s feet, then filled the broken opening with fire breath. The impact did not defeat the dragon. It gave the defenders a second in which to move, and Bowser used that second to run straight at Mimbus.

Fawthful stood between the broken window and the throne-room route. “Your castle falls soon. It belongs to us.”

“Over my dead Koopa shell,” Bowser said. “You are not taking my place without my permission. If I am not the Koopa King, no one is. This is my castle.”

Then Bowser turned away from the argument and shouted to the garrison.

“Get out of here! The dragon is coming! I do not want you getting smooshed!”

That order is the centre of the recovered battle. Bowser was still fighting for the castle, but he was no longer asking every defender to prove loyalty by standing in front of the dragon. He wanted the troops alive enough to be troops somewhere else.
sections.waluigi_note: An empty crown on a velvet cushion while two rival factions argue over who gets to sit in the brass chair.

sections.name: XIII. The Magikoopa Method
sections.overview:
The Magikoopas made the evacuation stranger and faster. They teleported Goombas around Mimbus so the small soldiers could flank the compromised route. One Goomba asked whether they were afraid. Goombas, after all, were always being stepped on by Mario.

“Nah,” the Goomba said. “It is just some dragons.”

At the window, a Hammer Bro protested that Bowser had ordered him to stay.

“I retract the order now,” Bowser told him. “Move.”

The Magikoopas began turning Goombas into blocks and tossing the blocks away from the line of attack. The defenders objected to the sight of their own troops being converted into masonry.

“We are transporting them,” a Magikoopa explained. “It is safer this way.”

The explanation did not make the method look safer. A flanking Goomba refused to cooperate. A hypnotised Koopa jumped for a flying brick and failed to catch it. Another Magikoopa, still loyal to Bowser, shouted that they might take the castle but they would not take their boss. The Magikoopas hovered, laughed at the confusion, and retreated with the people they could carry.

The evacuation was not clean. It was a series of bodies, blocks, teleports, and shouted corrections that kept the dragon from getting one uninterrupted target. That mattered more than dignity.
sections.waluigi_note: Geometric magic circles drawn in haste on floor tiles that were already buckling from subterranean heat.

sections.name: XIV. Mimbus, Cackletta, and the Claim
sections.overview:
Bowser swiped at Mimbus. Mimbus fell. The king looked at the breach and called for a retreat.

“What do you mean? We got this!” a Goomba protested.

“Have you ever fought a dragon before?” Bowser asked.

The Goomba had not.

Fawthful laughed, then sucked Cackletta into the vacuum apparatus as though removing a dangerous guest from a room. Fawthful climbed onto a hoverpad and rose above the broken floor.

“When people come to the castle, they will see me as the king,” Fawthful said. “I will be this world’s god.”

Fawthful claimed that half the castle had already been infiltrated and that Peach’s Castle was already under control. Bowser demanded to know why a bean wanted his castle.

“Power,” Fawthful answered. “I control the capital. You do not. I control the big Bowser Castle. You do not. Simple.”

Bowser’s answer was not reverent. It was administrative. Fawthful was not a king. Fawthful was renting a title without permission, and Bowser intended to take it back. Fawthful threatened to suck him up too.

The dragon struck the throne-room wall again.

“OWW! My head!”

The wall did not break. Fawthful stared at the dragon and demanded to know what kind of incompetent dragon had been supplied for the operation. The dragon tried to explain. Fawthful answered with the only management principle Fawthful seemed to possess: there would be consequences.
sections.waluigi_note: Signing a treaty in lightning while the building shook down to its bedrock foundations.

sections.name: XV. The Retreat Through the Broken Castle
sections.overview:
The remaining Hammer Bros began to retreat while they argued about the order. The hostile Koopas threw spears at them. One damaged a Koopa badly enough to make the difference between an orderly withdrawal and a rout visible to everyone in the courtyard.

“Do not kill them,” Bowser said. “They have caused me too much trouble to deal with. We are taking out the trash for now.”

The loyal Koopa troops paired their tactics. Shell barriers created a lane. Goombas pulled at legs and belts. The hypnotised soldiers were defeated by coordination rather than by one heroic strike. One Goomba tried to convince another that returning with him was better than being crushed alone.

“You will listen to me. I am the boss.”

The Goomba ran anyway.

The injured betrayer Koopas attempted to retreat with the rest. Bowser stopped them at the edge of the route.

“You cannot come.”

“Why?”

“You are traitors. You are lucky I am not killing you where I stand.”

The throne-room wall burst open before the argument could become a sentence. The dragon came through at last, wings sweeping the two traitors off the building. Bowser bolted into a side room with two Hammer Bros under his arms, carrying them the way a king carries equipment that has become unexpectedly alive.

The Hammer Bros gave their names as Fred and Ed. They had a question for him. Did the castle have a self-destruct switch? If the dragon was going to take the fortress, perhaps they could blow it up and move the survivors toward Neo Bowser City.

Bowser stopped.

“You want me to blow up my own castle?”

The Hammer Bros tried to explain that Mario had once pressed a switch and collapsed a castle. Bowser had not built that switch. If there had been one here, perhaps somebody had sabotaged it. The argument drifted toward the axe at the end of the river and the general problem of old castles containing controls nobody remembered installing.

Bowser rejected the plan. He wanted to leave before the dragon chomped them, but he also wanted Peach’s Castle checked and every survivor accounted for.

“Not just you imbeciles,” he clarified. “Everyone.”
sections.waluigi_note: Hauling wounded Koopas down spiral stone stairwells while steam hissed from ruptured boiler pipes.

sections.name: XVI. The Hag and the Switch
sections.overview:
Bowser ran into a hag at exactly the wrong moment. She had made a self-destruct switch and was pleased to present it.

“Who hired you?” Bowser asked.

“A green bean,” she said.

Bowser informed her that the castle was under siege and her duties had been relinquished. He asked what the switch controlled.

“I could have sworn it was the door,” she said.

Bowser pushed past her.

The switch therefore remained the same kind of exhibit as the earlier label promised: something that looked like a solution while making the evacuation more dangerous. Nobody could prove whether it destroyed the castle, opened a door, or merely added another joke to a room already full of them.

Outside, the dragon jumped on a brave Goomba and played with it until the play stopped being survivable. A small tear fell from one of the departing Magikoopas. The Magikoopas flew toward Neo Bowser City to carry the message that the castle had been breached and that the surviving force was retreating.
sections.waluigi_note: An elderly witch cackling over a junction box with copper wire in her teeth.

sections.name: XVII. Sir Frankfurt and the Dragon’s Question
sections.overview:
The dragon grew bored of the Goomba and turned its head toward another room. A Hammer Bro was still there, stiff with fear.

The dragon asked where Bowser was. The Hammer Bro answered that he was not the target. He was only guarding the room because Bowser had ordered him to stay, and then Bowser had retracted that order too late for the Hammer Bro to know where safety had gone.

The dragon admitted that it had been sent to kill Bowser in Draconic. The Hammer Bro answered in the same language that, since he was not the target, perhaps he could be released. The dragon considered the request. It had a bargain with the bean, but that did not mean it liked the bean. If the Hammer Bro could become useful to Bowser, that might be a better use of the dragon’s time than killing him.

The Hammer Bro did not want to die. He wanted to elevate Bowser’s kingdom. He said that Bowser had raised him when nobody else would. The dragon asked his name.

The Hammer Bro introduced himself as Sir Frankfurt, the fourteenth—or the fiftieth, depending on which part of the family count he reached first—and the tenth child of twenty-four. His father had charged Mario and died before the third world was over. His mother had died of grief a few days later. Bowser had taken in the surviving children. Bowser could be harsh, Sir Frankfurt said, but he had done right by them.

The dragon had heard enough family history. It called the speech nonsense and began to suck the Koopa into its vacuum. Sir Frankfurt grabbed the intake, curled into his shell, and spun. The shell struck the machine, vaulted upward, overshot the landing, and fell from the fifty-foot castle into the unknown.

The dragon looked after him, more shocked by the story than by the escape.
sections.waluigi_note: Asking an armored construct what its orders are while a dragon watches through the archway.

sections.name: XVIII. The Army That Was Not Bowser’s
sections.overview:
Elsewhere, a Goomba who had been watching the dragon talk to the Hammer Bro ran. He reached the route toward Toad Town Station, where the surviving force began making plans without the king.

There were nine Goombas and two Koopas. There were no magic users. One proposal was to raid Toad Town and turn it into Neo Bowser Town. Another was to go to Shy Guy Falls, because Shy Guys might be on Bowser’s side. A third involved stopping at Cheeseland for food because one of the Goombas liked cheese. The route was less an army plan than a frightened argument held over an empty train track.

“What if Mario comes and steps on us?” one Goomba asked.

Nobody knew where Mario was. Since Peach had died, the answer had always been that Mario was moving, missing, or both.

A small Fawthful drone appeared in the next room. The group had sent someone to tell Bowser that they had survived the dragon. The messenger had not returned. The drone had.

Then the other boss arrived: Koopa Killer Killa. The Goomba objected that Killa was not Bowser. Killa answered that Killa was the boss. Nobody had appointed Killa, but the empty space left by a retreating king was apparently enough to encourage the claim.

The group settled on Toad Town, then Shy Guy Falls, then Toad Town again, with the final decision depending on which sentence had been heard last. Everyone climbed toward the empty track.

A Hammer Bro remained behind the door because Bowser had ordered him to guard it. Killa demanded to know why he was still there. The Hammer Bro answered with the only command he still trusted: no one left behind. The Goomba said he would take his chances. The Hammer Bro stayed.

The Goomba walked toward the Fawthful drone. The fight began there, with the surviving army divided between a retreat it could not explain, a boss it had not chosen, and a machine that had been waiting for somebody to come close enough to attack.
sections.waluigi_note: Clockwork soldiers marching in perfect cadence with glowing yellow optical sensors.

sections.name: XIX. What This Scene Adds to the File
sections.overview:
The assault was not one clean charge from the outside. It began with the fake Bowser Jr. infiltration of the throne room and continued when the dragon broke into that same room. It was a chain of bad choices, loyal corrections, frightened improvisations, and competing definitions of who the boss was. Bowser’s retreat order saved bodies. The Magikoopas’ block transport made survival look ridiculous. The traitors were stopped but not erased. The Hammer Bros carried their own names into the evacuation. Sir Frankfurt’s story made the dragon hesitate, and the Fawthful drone found a remnant force that no longer knew which destination belonged to the king.

The historical record therefore ends on movement rather than victory. Bowser is trying to preserve the people and the castle’s future. Fawthful is trying to turn occupation into kingship and kingship into godhood. The dragon is following a contract it does not respect. The surviving Goombas and Koopas are trying to choose a route. The exact hour is unrecorded, but the sequence is clear: the false heir opened the inside, the dragon broke the outside, and the retreat exposed the people who would keep fighting after the castle stopped being one place.
sections.waluigi_note: A tactical post-mortem of how the greatest fortress in the Dark Lands changed hands before dawn. WAH.
